446f0fabeb1ae239: SEOUL: A hit song on the radio usually brings fame and fortune to its creator. But in South Korea, a recent chart-topper has instead blown open a massive legal headache for the entire music industry.
The track, Forest of the Heart, created by YouTuber Joseon HipHop, recently smashed its way into the Top 100 on Melon—Korea's biggest streaming platform.
According to The Korea Times, it quickly caught fire by word of mouth, particularly with older listeners.
The catch? The creator wrote the lyrics, but the melody and vocals were entirely generated by an AI platform called Suno.
While fans were humming along, music bosses were sweating.
The song's mainstream success has exposed a proper "regulatory vacuum"—a total lack of clear rules on who owns the rights to AI-assisted music and who gets paid the royalties.
The timing could not be worse. Just weeks before the song hit the charts, the Korea Music Copyright Association (KOMCA) tried to set up basic ground rules.
They briefly agreed to register AI-assisted tracks, provided a human made a proper creative contribution to the lyrics or arrangement.
Following massive pushback from government officials and the public, KOMCA pulled the plug on the new rules after just 22 days.
They cancelled the registrations, leaving musicians and producers completely in the dark.
According to government figures, thousands of songs submitted to copyright bodies already show signs of AI use.
Current Korean guidelines state that music created without human effort cannot be protected by copyright.
But nobody can agree on how much human input is actually needed to count as a "real" song.

Industry insiders warn that the sheer flood of AI tracks is already making a mess of the traditional music market. While countries like the US and Germany are drawing firmer lines on human authorship, South Korea is still playing catch-up.
With AI tunes climbing the charts, the real question is no longer whether AI music belongs in the mainstream—it is whether the law can move fast enough to keep up.
06c1d4cbca5ca6ac: KUALA LUMPUR: As the Malaysian men's team went down 3-2 after a titanic tussle against traditional rivals Indonesia in the last eight on Tuesday, shuttler Eogene Ewe has earned brickbats from netizens over his meek surrender in the decisive third singles.

Much was expected of the 21-year-old debutant, but after leading 4-0 at the beginning of the first game, the world No. 81 lost his way as 28th-ranked Zaki Ubaidillah cruised to a 21-11, 21-11 thrashing to take Indonesia into the last four.
"Eogene was once among Misbun's (Sidek) hopes, but after all these years, nothing seems to have developed," lamented a netizen.
Another fan was frustrated that Eogene looked like a novice against Zaki, despite the Indonesian being only 19 but having already won the Super 300 Thailand Masters this year.

"The level of the Indonesian men's singles player is far ahead of Malaysia's. Eogene looks like an MSSM (national school championships) player playing against them. He is already 21. Zaki is only 19, yet he is playing better than him," stated the fan on social media.
Another fan highlighted that mental strength is required when playing in team events, something Eogene lacked in a crunch situation at the Asian Games.

"Eogene was playing under pressure to win the game. When he tried too hard, he made more mistakes, and mentally he was not as strong as the young Indonesian player. It is a matter of mental strength when it comes to team tournaments," highlighted the fan.
One fan was unforgiving and said that Malaysian singles players are not as good as those from lesser-known badminton nations.
"He lost at the Sukma Games. Our singles players are on par with those from countries like Vietnam, the United States and Canada," stated the netizen.

There were also calls for rising star Kong Wei Xiang, who was a reserve in the team, to have been given a chance, as the 18-year-old had taken Olympic bronze medallist Antony Ginting to three games when Malaysia lost 3-2 to Indonesia in a group match of the Asian Team Championships earlier this year.

"It would have been better to let Kong Wei Xiang play. He was on the reserve list, and during the Asia Team Championships recently, he took (Antony) Ginting to three games as well," the netizen pointed out.

Eogene's inability to handle the pressure dented an improved performance from the singles players, with world No. 33 Leong Jun Hao toppling world No. 1 Jonatan Christie, while Justin Hoh suffered a close straight-game defeat to world No. 10 Alwi Farhan.

"At 21, he (Eogene) should be at the peak of his performance. The senior players we have are already nearing the end of their careers, and even their performances are inconsistent. Sometimes they are excellent, and sometimes they completely lose their way," said another commenter on social media, highlighting the current struggles of the national shuttlers over the past few years.

4a583d6ca07f251d: BANGI, Sept 23 — Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said he has yet to receive any motion of no confidence for the upcoming parliamentary sitting.

“Not even one (motion of no confidence) has been received. I have not heard anything about it,” he told reporters after officiating the ‘Negara Bangsa: Membina Jati Diri dan Identiti Nasional’ dialogue here today.

His remarks came after UMNO president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi challenged any party seeking to remove UMNO and Barisan Nasional (BN) from the Unity Government to formally do so by tabling a no-confidence motion in the Dewan Rakyat.
Johari also said he had yet to receive the proposed Bills on the separation of the roles of the Attorney General and Public Prosecutor, as well as the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure.

“I was informed that there were plans for them, but I have yet to receive the papers. Usually, two weeks before the tabling, the Speaker will be informed. But so far, I have not received anything,” he said.

Earlier, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the Bill to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure was ready to be tabled in the upcoming parliamentary session.

According to the Dewan Rakyat calendar on the Parliament website, the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament will run for 37 days from Oct 5 to Dec 8, with Budget 2027 scheduled to be tabled on Oct 9. — Bernama

e8ba8a81c4989b36: SHAH ALAM: The 15-year-old teen who fatally stabbed his 16-year-old schoolmate at a school in Bandar Utama last year had watched her heading for the toilet during an examination before following her there.
According to the grounds of judgement by High Court judge Adlin Abdul Majid, the boy saw the girl heading towards the female washroom on the lower floor and followed her before entering the washroom.
The judgment said the teen confronted the deceased at knifepoint and led her to the second cubicle.
"Once inside the cubicle, he locked the door, proceeded to ask the deceased whether she was (her name) and told her that he liked her.
"She resisted and attempted to leave, and he pushed her back and began stabbing her.

"An autopsy report dated Dec 22, 2025 prepared by Dr Koo Zhao Peng, a medical practitioner at the Universiti Malaya Medical Centre forensic pathology department recorded a very large number of stab and incise wounds - in the region of 180 to 200 in total- at various parts of the deceased's body.
"The deceased died in cubicle 2 from multiple stab wounds to the neck and chest.
"The wounds causing the deceased's death were inflicted by the child, using a knife measuring approximately 30cm, with the word "Leatherneck SF" inscribed on the blade," said the judgment.
On Sept 14, Adlin acquitted the boy of murdering the deceased after she found him to be of unsound mind during the incident on Oct 14 last year.
She ordered the boy to be detained and treated at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta in Perak at the pleasure of the Sultan of Selangor.

b8c9566e2f8a41c0: NEW YORK: The future of artificial intelligence and the stalled US war against Iran, with its ripple effect on the global economy, are expected to dominate the UN gathering of world leaders Wednesday.
Following weeks of worldwide headlines about risks of uncontrollable AI – and calls for a slowdown – industry leaders are set to brief an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council.
Sam Altman of OpenAI, Dario Amodei of Anthropic and Clement Delangue of Hugging Face will brief the 15-strong Council, the United Nation's top body.

Hugging Face, a repository of AI models, was the target of a recent cyberattack by autonomous OpenAI software, the first in a series of incidents that have raised alarm bells over the rapidly evolving technology.

Meanwhile, the annual parade of UN General Assembly speeches is set to continue, with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian arriving late Tuesday, according to Iranian state media, to address the world body for the first time since the United States and Israel launched attacks on his country.
The strikes in late February sparked a war that engulfed the Middle East, and the Trump administration has so far yet to reach a deal with Teheran to end the conflict.
Teheran retaliated by blocking the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for energy transit, sparking a surge in global oil prices.
The recent Houthi takeover of Yemen's Red Sea coast has also heightened fears over global trade and shipping through the vital Bab al-Mandab Strait.

Pezeshkian's speech will come a day after Trump raised the possibility that he could "annihilate the Islamic Republic" and "drive them into hell." During his remarks, all but one member of the Iranian delegation walked out.
Trump made the comments in a fire and brimstone speech Tuesday, but he also revealed that there were talks between the two sides for the first time in months.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Trump's roving envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner on the sidelines of the UN's signature diplomatic gathering.

Araghchi said that Teheran's demands included "the immediate lifting of the (US) naval blockade, the prompt payment of all Iranian assets that have been frozen, and an end to the war on all resistance fronts," state news agency IRIB reported.
Outside the UN on Tuesday, there was a vigil with protesters demonstrating against Teheran's use of the death penalty.
Besides conflict in the Middle East, Russia's war against Ukraine will again be raised among global diplomatic circles on Wednesday.
A Security Council meeting on Ukraine is scheduled for 11am (1500 GMT), while President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is due to address the UN General Assembly as well.
Zelenskyy, after meeting with Trump on Tuesday, said that Washington and Kyiv want the war with Russia to end "before winter."
He added that he is ready to halt strikes on Russian energy sites if Moscow agreed to do the same.
In his speech Tuesday, Trump rejected international regulation of AI, calling such proposals a "globalist scheme."
"The very same people who said we'll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming... are now saying that AI is going to kill us all," Trump said.
But just hours after Trump spoke, Macron took to the rostrum and defiantly called for the creation of an open-source AI model not dependent on the United States or China.
"I don't want anyone to become the vassal of one of the great powers," he said.
"Rather, we must come together to build an open-source frontier model, a cutting-edge model."

73c3f20f806cad2c: TEHRAN, Sept 23 — Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian arrived in New York where he is expected to speak at the United Nations General Assembly, Iranian state media reported today.

State broadcaster IRIB posted a video clip of Pezeshkian exiting a plane with a caption saying that the Iranian president has arrived at a New York airport. This is the first time that a leader whose country is at war with the US sets foot on American soil to address a UN gathering, analysts say. — AFP
fd01f5d1229f9ad4: KUCHING, Sept 23 — Two men aged 40 and 23 were remanded for three days by the Magistrates’ Court here today to assist investigations into a case of mischief by fire involving a convenience store along Jalan Green here.
Senior Court Registrar Syazwani Sajeli allowed the remand application after hearing submissions by investigating officer Insp Tan Chiang Fook and their counsel Daniel Ling.
The court ordered both suspects to be remanded for three days from Sept 23 to Sept 26 to assist investigations under Section 436 of the Penal Code.
It was reported that the incident occurred at the premises in Jalan Green, Sin Sin Park here at about 8.30pm on Sept 20.
The 40-year-old suspect was arrested at a premises in Sibu at about 2.40pm on Sept 22, while the other was arrested later the same day at about 9.30pm at a cafe along Jalan Nanas, Sarikei.
The case is one of two incidents of mischief by fire reported in Kuching and Sri Aman on Sept 20, involving premises belonging to the same convenience store chain.
Three suspects have been arrested and remanded to assist investigations into both incidents. — The Borneo Post
3d147ca3195be840: GEORGE TOWN: JustGO is now available on Penang Bridge, giving motorists another digital option for paying tolls through automatic number plate recognition (ANPR).
Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the implementation marked another step towards digitalising the country's transport and toll payment systems.
He said the system would provide a smoother and more flexible experience, particularly for Penang residents who use the bridge daily.
"With JustGO, registered users can drive through the toll plaza without having to choose a lane based on a specific payment method," he said.
The ANPR system detects a vehicle's registration number, while toll transactions are automatically processed using the payment card linked to the JustGO application.
Zairil said the system's LaneFreedom feature allowed users to use any available toll lane on Penang Bridge.
However, at the Bandar Cassia toll plaza, JustGO is currently available only at designated RFID lanes marked with a red circle.
Penang residents who register through JustGO will also enjoy a 20 per cent discount on Penang Bridge tolls, he added.
"ANPR technology is expected to help improve traffic flow at toll plazas, reduce reliance on physical payment methods and support Penang's aspiration to become a smart state," he said.
Users can access JustGO through the Apple App Store, Google Play or Huawei AppGallery, then register their account and vehicle before linking a payment card.
Users are advised that payment notifications may arrive shortly after passing through a toll plaza as ANPR transactions may require additional verification.
Complete transaction records, including the time and location of each journey, can be checked through the JustGO application.
The state government encourages Penang Bridge users to adopt the new payment option as part of efforts to improve daily mobility through digital technology.
561b9831d4082e16: KUCHING, Sept 23 — Lubok Antu moved out of the very unhealthy category by noon today after its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading dropped from 205 at 8am to 195.
The improvement left Kanowit as the only station in Sarawak recording a very unhealthy reading at noon, with its API at 208, down from 244 at 8am.
Despite the improvement, Lubok Antu remained in the unhealthy category, according to the latest API readings from the Natural Resources and Environment Board (NREB) Status for Sarawak.
Most monitoring stations across Sarawak also remained in the unhealthy category at noon, with readings ranging from 105 to 195.
Serian recorded the highest unhealthy reading at 186, followed by Sri Aman at 180, Betong at 178, Belaga at 174 and Samarahan at 173.
Kuching registered 179, while Bintulu was at 170, Sarikei 168, Sibu 167, Miri 161 and Samalaju 162.
Other readings included ILP Miri at 158, Tebedu 159, Mukah and Limbang 153 each, Lundu 128, Lawas 129 and Kapit 121.
Bario was the only station outside the unhealthy and very unhealthy categories, recording a moderate reading of 74 at noon compared with 33 at 8am.
Under the API classification, readings of 0–50 are considered good, 51–100 moderate, 101–200 unhealthy and 201–300 very unhealthy. — The Borneo Post
b37f71d8f8ca4c07: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia needs to invest in sovereign space technology and infrastructure to keep critical communications and data under local control, while positioning the country for the next wave of digital and economic growth, according to Measat Satellite Systems.
The satellite operator is calling for the 2027 Budget to make sovereign SpaceTech a national investment priority as Malaysia seeks to grow its space industry revenue beyond RM10 billion by 2030.

Measat chief operating officer Yau Chyong Lim said the country's space sector generated RM6.2 billion in revenue between 2017 and 2024, with the rollout of Malaysia Space Exploration 2030 (MSE2030) from 2027 to 2030 providing an opportunity to turn that growth into a larger economic and technology ecosystem.

He said Malaysia's ability to control critical space assets, communications infrastructure and data would be increasingly important to national resilience, economic competitiveness and strategic independence.
He said Measat has established end-to-end sovereign satellite connectivity capabilities that keep critical national communications, infrastructure and data under Malaysian control.

For the 2027 Budget, Yau said the company proposed five priorities: strengthening sovereign space capabilities; supporting long-term investment in space infrastructure; accelerating integrated SpaceTech applications; helping local companies commercialise space technologies; and developing specialised research and talent.

Among the proposals are stronger local ownership and participation in national space programmes, investment frameworks suited to the long development cycles of space infrastructure and greater public-private partnerships in multi-orbit platforms and nationally governed data systems.

He said Measat also wants Malaysia to integrate geostationary Earth orbit, low Earth orbit and terrestrial networks, while expanding satellite-enabled applications in disaster management, maritime surveillance, precision agriculture, rural healthcare and smart infrastructure.

He added that the 2027 Budget should also support locally developed SpaceTech solutions, start-ups and research institutions, while creating pathways for Malaysian companies to access regional and international markets.

Yau also called for stronger industry-academia collaboration and investment in local expertise spanning engineering, telecommunications, artificial intelligence, data analytics, remote sensing and space regulation.
He said Malaysia already has key foundations, including sovereign orbital rights and spectrum resources, satellites, ground infrastructure, engineering expertise and regulatory capabilities.
"These priorities will build on existing strengths while supporting the aspiration of MSE2030 and Dasar Angkasa Negara 2030," he said.
a014d405fc2f59f4: SHANGHAI: Chinese automakers grabbed another record share of Europe’s car market last month, luring buyers still wary about going fully electric with more affordable hybrid vehicles.

Brands including BYD made up nearly 12% of total new-car sales in the region in August, according to Dataforce. They accounted for one in four sales of all hybrids — or one in three for hybrids with a plug — as they cash in on models that aren’t subject to steep European Union tariffs.

The data show how China’s carmakers are capitalising on lingering consumer concern around charging networks and driving range, with hybrids acting as a stepping-stone to going fully electric. Still, surging fuel prices are piling pressure on the finances of combustion-engine car owners.
Demand for battery and hybrid cars jumped 27% in August, according to Dataforce, to offset declines for vehicles that only run on fuel. Thanks to EV gains, the overall market rose 4.6%.

Chinese hybrid vehicles don’t currently face the same steep European Union tariffs as electric-vehicle imports from the country, though they may soon be hit with similar duties, Handelsblatt has reported. Germany is preparing a package of economic security measures that may include new tariffs on hybrids which it plans to present to the EU, Bloomberg reported this month.

In the UK, Chinese carmakers don’t face the additional tariffs on EVs currently in place in the EU. There, more than one in five new cars is Chinese, with brands like Chery Automobile’s Jaecoo proving a hit with consumers.
While volumes aren’t as high in Germany, Chinese companies are also gaining ground in Europe’s largest car market, picking up a 6.4% market share there in August, according to Dataforce.
“Even if their market share is comparably low to other markets, the sheer size of the German market makes that move however very attractive,” said Dataforce analyst Julian Litzinger.

Across Europe, EV sales are climbing, in part due to the return of incentives in countries like Germany. That’s taking a toll on some European manufacturers because those models tend to have lower margins. Volkswagen AG last week said the uplift is weighing on profitability, particularly at the Volkswagen passenger-car and Audi brands.

The Paris car show next month will give European brands an opportunity to showcase their fightback on home turf. For Chinese marques, it’s a chance to lay out plans to target the premium end of the market, having already made inroads with mass-market buyers.
45783492aa891933: KUALA LUMPUR: The Alliance for a Safe Community (Ikatan) has called for stronger mental health support for civil servants after 55,169 were identified as high risk in a mental health screening exercise.
It said officers identified as being at risk should receive confidential, professional and timely support, with appropriate referral for further assessment where necessary.
The non-governmental organisation said psychological wellbeing should be a workplace safety and occupational health priority.

Ikatan also called for managers and department heads to be trained to recognise warning signs and respond appropriately to stress, burnout, anxiety, depression, workplace bullying and other psychosocial risks without stigmatising or punishing affected employees.

The group said greater focus should also be placed on prevention, with workload, long working hours, workplace bullying, inadequate staffing, poor work-life balance and organisational culture examined where they contribute to psychological distress.

It said every ministry and agency should have a clear mental health action plan, including access to trained psychological support, peer-support mechanisms, regular psychosocial risk assessments and clear pathways for urgent intervention.

On Monday, Public Service Department (PSD) deputy director-general (Development) Datuk Dr Mohd Bakhari Ismail said 55,169 civil servants had been categorised as officers with a high risk of suicidal tendencies.
Bakhari said the figure highlighted the importance of strengthening psychological wellbeing among civil servants.
823cd297cc3cc581: KUALA LUMPUR: Paragon Globe Bhd is expanding beyond conventional property development by focusing on creating economic ecosystems around its strategic landbank in Johor.

While property development remains its core business, Paragon Globe said it is increasingly evaluating land based on the economic activity, community and long-term value that can be created around each location.

The strategy spans industrial, residential, commercial and income-generating developments, with Paragon Globe focusing on attracting suitable uses and anchor occupiers into strategic growth corridors.

Paragon Globe has proposed a RM398.11 million land disposal in Tanjung Kupang to a data centre infrastructure player, while nearby land is being developed around the PGB-GSP AutoPark automotive ecosystem.
According to its executive chairman Datuk Sri Edwin Tan Pei Seng, the two uses reflect PGB's approach of placing different economic activities within the same wider growth corridor.
"One brings digital infrastructure. Another brings automotive manufacturing and potentially its supporting supply chain.
"We are not simply buying and selling parcels independently. We try to put the right users into the right locations and create stronger economic activity around the area," said Tan.
At the same time, Paragon Globe is rebuilding its longer-term development pipeline.

In Sedenak, within the Kulai-Sedenak flagship zone of the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), the company is pursuing a substantial land position that could support a preliminary RM1.69 billion industrial park concept comprising industrial factories, commercial components and worker accommodation.

Moving forward, Paragon Globe will focus on strategic landbank management, ecosystem-led development, disciplined capital allocation and timely project execution as it builds its presence across Johor's key growth corridors.

"We will continue to invest, but we do not need to fund every project at the same time. We phase our developments, recycle capital where it makes sense and adjust our timing if market conditions change," Tan said.
bf41befacfb363fc: PETALING JAYA, Sept 23 — Malaysia’s property market remains soft, with growth appearing moderate despite a marginal improvement in sales performance during the first half of 2026, according to the Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) Malaysia.

Presenting the findings of the Property Industry Survey (PIS) at Wisma Rehda today, Rehda president Datuk Zaini Yusoff said that while the industry is seeing some activity, the market continues to grapple with unsold inventory and financing challenges.
The survey found that 59 per cent of respondents had unsold stock as of June 30.

Data from the survey showed that the number of units launched remained broadly unchanged, with 15,834 units entering the market in the first half (1H) of 2026 compared with 15,841 units in the second half (2H) of 2025 — a difference of just seven units.
However, sales performance saw a modest uptick, with 5,260 units sold, representing a 3.2 per cent increase from the 5,098 units recorded in the previous six-month period.
Consequently, the overall take-up rate edged up to 33.2 per cent from 32.2 per cent in 2H 2025.
"Performance remained mixed across property types, indicating that the market continues to remain soft," Zaini said during the presentation.
According to the report, apartments and condominiums were the strongest-performing property type, recording a take-up rate of 58 per cent, followed by semi-detached and cluster homes at 30 per cent.
In terms of volume, apartments and condominiums accounted for the highest number of units sold at 3,032, followed by serviced residences at 1,114 and two-to-three-storey terrace houses at 610.
The survey found that the majority of launches, at 53 per cent, were priced between RM300,001 and RM500,000, primarily in Perak, Pahang and Negeri Sembilan.
Only one per cent of units were priced at RM2.5 million and above.
Meanwhile, the market remained heavily skewed towards domestic demand, with 98 per cent of buyers being Malaysians.
Foreigners accounted for just two per cent of sales, indicating that international demand remained limited.
Younger buyers dominated the market, with 70 per cent of purchasers aged between 29 and 44.
The hurdle of unsold units
Despite the marginal increase in sales, the Rehda survey highlighted persistent concerns over unsold completed residential units, with 59 per cent of respondents reporting such stock as of June 30.
The top three reasons cited for units remaining unsold were end-financing loan rejections at 30 per cent, high pricing at 21 per cent and unreleased Bumiputera units at 16 per cent.
Notably, 33 per cent of these unsold completed units were priced at RM1 million and above.
Zaini said the issue of end-financing remained critical.

"Among the main factors contributing to housing loan rejection were purchasers’ income eligibility, lower margins of financing offered by financial institutions, and applicants’ adverse credit histories, suggesting the continuing importance of access to appropriate end-financing in supporting home ownership," he said.
The survey involved 181 Rehda members and focused on property market performance across Peninsular Malaysia.

Conducted by the Rehda Institute between July and August 2026, the survey aimed to evaluate market performance in the first half of 2026 while providing an outlook for the second half of 2026 and the first half of 2027.
4d00705512461450: SEOUL: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and US President Donald Trump welcomed "significant progress" in discussions on strategic investment projects during a 30-minute meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Seoul's presidential office said on Wednesday.

The meeting came after South Korea's industry ministry briefed lawmakers on Tuesday on implementation plans under the country's US$350 billion investment package, including a Texas gas-fired power project identified as a potential first investment, as well as possible investments in nuclear energy and an Alaska LNG project.
"The two leaders welcomed the significant progress made in discussions on strategic investment projects between the two countries," national security adviser Wi Sung-lac told a briefing.

Based on the Joint Fact Sheet issued after their summit last November, Lee and Trump also agreed to deepen cooperation and continue discussions on issues including nuclear fuel enrichment and reprocessing, nuclear-powered submarines, shipbuilding and the transfer of wartime operational control (OPCON) from the US to South Korea, Wi said.
Trump also reaffirmed his willingness to engage in dialogue with North Korea, Wi said, with the two leaders agreeing to remain in close communication in pursuit of a peace process.

Lee also said the US-China summit scheduled for Thursday would be important for regional developments, including South Korea-China relations, and expressed hope for a successful meeting, according to Wi.
The White House did not immediately comment on the Trump-Lee meeting.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio on Friday called for the swift execution of South Korean investment commitments during a meeting with South Korean foreign minister Cho Hyun, the state department said.
Discussed North Korea, golf

Earlier on Wednesday, Lee told the UN General Assembly that Seoul would support efforts to revive dialogue with North Korea and work toward a durable peace framework while seeking broader international backing for those efforts.

A senior presidential official separately told South Korean media outlets that Lee had told Trump he hoped the US president would help advance engagement with North Korea, to which Trump replied that he would do so.

The official said Trump also remarked that he maintained a good relationship with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, though there was no indication of any specific contact currently taking place, the media reports said.

The official said Lee and Trump also spent considerable time discussing OPCON transfer, with Trump gaining a better understanding of Seoul's position. The US side stressed the need to meet the required conditions and complete the process as soon as possible, the reports said.
The South Korean side outlined plans to increase defence spending while expressing a desire to accelerate talks on Seoul's plans to develop nuclear-powered submarines, the official said.
The two sides agreed to hold follow-up consultations on the various issues in Washington as soon as possible, the reports said.
The official was also quoted as saying that progress in talks on South Korean investments in US projects helped pave the way for the summit, which had not initially been expected to take place.
The two leaders had been briefed on the negotiations and welcomed the progress, but discussions were still under way on the details of the package and how it would be announced, the official said.
"The bigger framework is almost complete," the official was quoted as saying.
Trump raised the prospect of playing golf with Lee, who suggested the two could play on the sidelines of a G20 summit in Miami in December, the official said.
The pair previously discussed playing golf during their meeting at the G7 summit in France in June.
9020a874f483c084: BEIJING: Chinese tech giant Alibaba unveiled plans on Wednesday to expand its overseas data centres, targeting markets across Europe and the Middle East.
Hangzhou-based Alibaba is one of the frontrunners in China's artificial intelligence industry, with its Qwen model among the world's most downloaded AI models.

The company said it would "establish its first cloud regions" in Turkey, Finland and the Netherlands, while "expanding its data centre footprint in Malaysia, Germany, the United Arab Emirates, France and Hong Kong" over the next 12 months.

The announcement came ahead of a highly anticipated meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and his US counterpart Donald Trump in Washington, where the two leaders are expected to discuss trade tensions, among other topics.
Beijing and Washington are locked in a tech rivalry increasingly centred on frontier industries, including semiconductors, AI and robotics.

Alibaba chief executive officer Eddie Wu said on Tuesday that the company was planning to train an AI model with five to 10 trillion parameters, which would make it several times bigger than the current largest Chinese model.

cafeef683e3ecba1: KUALA LUMPUR: Residents of Block D at Pangsapuri Damai Perdana were caught off-guard when a slope near their apartment gave way last night.
Muhammad Fitri Abu Seman, 35, said he and his mother-in-law, Anum Shariff, 73, first noticed the landslide at about 8.48pm while having drinks at a restaurant opposite the apartment.
He said what had initially been a quiet evening quickly turned tense when they realised that part of the slope near the apartment had collapsed.
They immediately contacted the Fire and Rescue Department to report the incident and seek assistance.
"This is the first time something like this has happened at this apartment.
"There was previously a landslide reported at a secondary school located near the apartment," he said when met today.
Fitri said he and his family had no plans to leave their home for now as they had not been instructed by the authorities to do so.
"For now, we are staying at home because our block has not been badly affected. We are more comfortable staying at home," he said.

He hoped the local authority could arrange an alternative water supply for residents after the main water pipe was temporarily shut off to prevent water flow from contributing to further soil movement.
Another resident, Muhammad Syakir Nabil Azman, 32, said he rushed home after receiving a call from his wife informing him of the landslide near their home.
"My wife called and told me to come home quickly. She said people downstairs were shouting for everyone to get out because there had been a landslide.
"I immediately rushed home and took my wife and child out of the house," he said.
Syakir, who has lived at the apartment for the past two years, said his wife managed to pack essential belongings before the family temporarily moved to his mother-in-law's home in Taman Tun Perak.
He said they did not feel any tremors or movement in the building during the incident.
Instead, they saw muddy water gushing from the landslide area.
"There was no shaking at all. We could only see water coming from the soil. It was really like a waterfall," he said.
It was reported that residents living near a slope at an apartment complex in Bandar Damai Perdana, Cheras, were ordered to evacuate last night after a landslide occurred close to the building.

Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 9.03pm regarding the incident near Block D of the Damai Perdana Apartment.
The landslide is believed to have been caused by an underground water leak.

0defb2419be23766: PERTH/SINGAPORE: Oil prices extended declines on Wednesday as investors eyed improved Gulf supply after Saudi Arabia restarted operations at a critical pipeline.
Hopes for a diplomatic solution to the US-Iran war also weighed on prices.
Brent crude futures fell US$1.09, or 1.1 per cent, to US$98.16 a barrel as of 0421 GMT, while West Texas Intermediate futures fell US$1.50, or 1.67 per cent, to US$89.01 per barrel.
Both contracts have declined for six consecutive sessions to around two-week lows.

While US President Donald Trump warned on Tuesday that he could "annihilate" Iran, he also said his envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had held productive talks with mediators of Iran to end the war.
"I think there's a lot of momentum for them to make a deal," Trump said.
Optimism around improved supply and a push to end the nearly seven-month conflict drove benchmark Brent down to close below US$100 a barrel on Tuesday for the first time since September 8.
"The market is currently feeling more constructive about the global oil supply picture than it was a few weeks ago," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade.

"The meeting of US and Iranian delegations in New York has given traders a glimmer of hope ... Despite the continued tough rhetoric, including threats of 'annihilation', the market is choosing to price in the possibility of talks."
On Tuesday, Saudi Arabia restarted operations on its East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea, three sources briefed on the matter said, with signs of an increase in Middle Eastern oil flows.
Drone attacks, which Saudi Arabia has blamed on Iraqi militia, forced the kingdom to shut the pipeline on September 11, halting crude loadings at the kingdom's Yanbu port.

Since the US-Israeli war on Iran disrupted oil flows from Saudi Arabia and its Gulf neighbours through the Strait of Hormuz, Riyadh has been using the pipeline to reroute around 4.0 million barrels per day — around 4.0 per cent of global supply — to Yanbu.
Saudi also offered more barrels to Asian refiners for lifting from locations outside of the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday.

Iraq, too, is increasing oil exports, its oil minister, Basim Mohammed, said on Tuesday. The country is exporting more than 3.0 million bpd, he said, and expects to boost exports via Turkey to more than 600,000 bpd.

Provisional data from shiptracking firms Vortexa and Kpler pegged Iraqi crude exports in August at 2.3 million and 2.17 million bpd, respectively, up from July's level but below February's pre-war level of 3.7 million and 3.362 million bpd.
Adding to downward pressure on oil prices, industry data showed US crude inventories rose by 1.8 million barrels in the week to September 18. Analysts polled by Reuters had expected a decline.

e8a5979e99df5751: SAN FRANCISCO, Sept 23 — The most powerful venture capital firm in Silicon Valley is starting a two-year private school for young people intended to replace college, as some US tech elite question the benefits of a classical university education.

The Horowitz Andreessen Academy, or HAA, is backed by veteran investors Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, two towering figures of the US tech industry and founders of venture capital giant Andreessen Horowitz.

The announcement said students would hear lectures from tech leaders including Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, Microsoft chief Satya Nadella, Uber founder Travis Kalanick and former OpenAI executive Mira Murati.
It framed San Francisco itself as central to the project, describing the city as unusually open to newcomers and a hub for innovation.

"We think this can be an elite institution that attracts top-tier talent — one that prepares students for the future rather than remaining stuck in the past," the academy's CEO, Gagan Biyani, said on X.
The venture has raised US$42 million from investors, including Shopify chief executive Tobi Lutke, DoorDash chief executive Tony Xu, and former Instacart chief and OpenAI executive Fidji Simo.
"We live in an age of infinite knowledge, and we are entering an age of infinite doing," the academy said in its launch announcement.

Biyani said the program would replace lecture-heavy coursework with independent, business-oriented projects, describing the model as closer to Oxford's tutorial system or the Montessori method than a conventional university.

Some of the tech industry's most celebrated founders never finished college — Microsoft's Bill Gates and Facebook's Mark Zuckerberg both left Harvard, while Apple's Steve Jobs dropped out of Reed College.
This history is often invoked in Silicon Valley to argue that a degree is not a prerequisite for building a major company, and that young entrepreneurs should not waste time in the classroom.

The academy joins a growing list of venture-backed efforts to position elite young talent outside traditional four-year degree programs, often on the grounds that US campuses are too liberal or anti-business.

The Thiel Fellowship, founded by right-wing billionaire investor Peter Thiel in 2011, pays selected young people to skip or leave college and build companies instead. Its current fellows receive US$250,000 over two years.
Anthropic, Coinbase, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI, Palantir, Replit and Stripe are among more than 30 companies Biyani described as partners.
They will offer students work experience, advice and computing credits in exchange for early access to talent.
Applications are open for a tuition-free pilot year of 50 students starting in September 2027.
This will precede the eventual two-year, paid version of the program, which Biyani said would be similar in cost to an elite private university.
Annual tuition at Stanford University, in the heart of Silicon Valley, stands at US$67,731 for the 2026-27 academic year, not including room and board. — AFP
319ee9733656455e: PETALING JAYA, Sept 23 — The 15-year-old boy who killed his female schoolmate at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year had come to view the victim and those around him as “NPCs”, the Shah Alam High Court was told.

In gaming terminology, an NPC — or non‑player character — refers to background characters controlled by the game rather than by a human player, and the term is sometimes used online to imply that a person lacks agency or individuality.

In her full grounds of judgment, Judge Adlin Abdul Majid said this was disclosed in a psychiatric report prepared by Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony, the director and senior consultant forensic psychiatrist at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta.

In disclosing his findings, Dr Ian highlighted the existence of a “Death Note” journal on the accused’s mobile phone, in which he repeatedly referred to the deceased while chronicling the disturbing and psychotic thoughts in his mind.

Death Note is a Japanese anime and manga series centred on a student who discovers a supernatural notebook that allows him to kill anyone by writing their name, and the character Kira — whom the accused identified with — is portrayed as a vigilante who believes he has the authority to judge and eliminate others.
The journal, written in Mandarin, contained accounts of his symptoms six months before the murder.

“The entries show persecutory beliefs that classmates were conspiring against him and deserved to die, a wish for mass casualties, and a conviction that others would lie to the police to make him appear at fault.
“They show his dehumanisation of those around him, most starkly in his adoption of the term NPC to describe his schoolmates as subhuman, valueless game objects.

“They show a grandiose delusion of having become Kira, a godlike figure entitled to judge and eliminate others, and open identification with Eric Harris, Dylan Klebold and other mass killers as role models and (in his own words) as gods,” she said in her grounds.

Adlin said the entries further showed the evolution of his fixation on the deceased, from professed love to an intention to take her with him in death, alongside pervasive suicidal thoughts, profound loneliness and a belief that his self-worth was entirely tied to his physical appearance.
Psychiatric report findings

The psychiatric report also noted a strong family history of mental illness, including an institutionalised aunt, a mentally disordered paternal grand-uncle and two affected sons, as well as a family member treated for depression.
Dr Ian further said that the child’s situation worsened over the years as he was exposed to the internet, video games and anime.

The report said that from around 2020, when the child was nine and during the Covid-19 movement control period, his family and later teachers observed a gradual change in his behaviour, with him becoming withdrawn, isolating himself in his room and refusing to communicate with his family.
“He also developed a persistent belief that he was physically unattractive and that other students were laughing at and talking about him.
“He began wearing a face mask at all times, even after public health requirements had ended, refusing to remove it to eat or drink at school.”
Outside home, he became highly anxious and believed people were observing him, which the report described as paranoid delusions.

The psychiatric report identified a further evolution of psychotic symptoms in 2023, when he became suspicious that CCTV cameras had been secretly installed in his home and believed he was being watched by ‘the eye’ of a technician who had repaired the system.
The report described this as a paranoid delusion, reinforced by his perception of a red light in his room, which was recorded as a visual hallucination.
“He later became convinced that his parents had covertly installed cameras in his room and bathroom.

“By early 2025, the belief had extended to his school, where he believed the security guard and certain teachers were secretly monitoring him via CCTV, including while he was in the school washroom,” the report added.
Dr Ian also said the accused began developing an interest in school shooters and serial killers, while from around August 2024, he developed an infatuation with the deceased.

Seven months before the murder, Dr Ian noted that the accused began experiencing auditory hallucinations in the form of a voice he attributed to Dylan Klebold, speaking to him in Mandarin and instructing him to kill the deceased.
Around the same period, the accused also began identifying with Light Yagami, or Kira, the god-like vigilante from Death Note.
“Taken as a whole, I accept that this chronology reflects a serious and longstanding psychotic illness that developed and worsened progressively over several years.

“By the time of the incident, the child was in the grip of an active psychosis, marked by delusions directed at the deceased and a commanding hallucinated voice instructing him to kill her,” Adlin said.

She said Dr Ian’s testimony rejected the suggestion that the accused had feigned his symptoms, with the journal entries confirming that the psychotic beliefs described in the psychiatric report were not constructed for the trial but were genuinely present in the boy’s mind in the period leading up to the incident.

Adlin said that three weeks after being prescribed antipsychotic medication, Dr Ian testified that the accused’s hallucinations had ceased and his delusions had begun to dissolve, while he also began engaging warmly with his family in a manner not seen for years.

In fact, the illness’s severity was well documented, with Dr Ian stating that the accused had experienced a wide range of psychiatric symptoms for about five years without receiving medical treatment by the time the offence occurred, including severe and debilitating psychotic symptoms in the form of hallucinations and delusions.
“Based on the evidence set out in the psychiatric report, DW2 (Dr Ian) diagnosed the child with schizophrenia, of very early onset (before the age of 13) with psychopathic and sadistic traits.

During cross-examination, Adlin said DW2 drew an important distinction between hallucinations and delusions, explaining that hallucinations are intermittent and come and go, whereas delusions are fixed and continuously present.
“On this basis, the delusional system was not something that came upon the child occasionally. It was present throughout, including during the incident,” she said.

Adlin also noted that DW2 explained the clinical significance of the accused having remained untreated for five years, noting that this period, known as the duration of untreated psychosis (DUP), is measured from the onset of symptoms to the start of medication.
“The Malaysian mean DUP is 28.7 months, compared with approximately 60 months in the child’s case.

“DW2 then elaborated that untreated psychosis does not remain static — it becomes more elaborate over time, and the longer it goes unchallenged, the more internally logical it becomes to the person experiencing it, and the more resistant to correction.
“As such, by the time of the incident, the child’s reality testing was impaired to the point that the world he perceived was not the world the rest of us live in,” she said.
92ce81d509a37aaf: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hailed Malaysia’s 22 young competitors at the 48th WorldSkills Competition here as the country’s pride, stressing that skilled workers are indispensable to a modern, technology-driven economy.
“You have spent years practising something difficult until you could do it well. Whatever the result this week, your country is proud of you.

“Your participation here lets Malaysia test itself against the best in the world. It shows us how our standards compare and where we can improve,” he said at the plenary session of the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 Conference and Expo here today.

Malaysia is represented by 22 young competitors across 21 skill areas at the competition, which brings together about 1,400 young professionals from more than 65 countries and regions, marking the country’s continued participation in the event since 1995.

Touching on youth’s role in the economy, Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said young skilled workers play a crucial role in keeping modern economies running, even as machinery and software become increasingly sophisticated.
“A modern economy cannot function without the technicians who keep a semiconductor line running or an electric vehicle plant on schedule.
“The machinery may become more sophisticated. The software may become more intelligent. But somebody still has to understand how it works and know what to do when it does not,” he said.
Anwar said young people would be drawn to technical and skilled professions if they could see clear prospects for career advancement and better livelihoods.
“Our task is to make sure that it leads somewhere worth going: to skilled work and good incomes. Skill of that depth is built slowly,” said the Prime Minister.

Citing an old Chinese saying that it takes 10 years to grow a tree but 100 years to cultivate a person, Anwar said the energy and dynamism of young people were pivotal to economic progress, and that society must move beyond viewing youth merely as contributors to material and economic advancement.
“There isn’t any doubt that the energy and vibrancy of young people contributes substantively to high productivity in this pursuit of material wealth,” he said.
Anwar said young people also make significant contributions to society, including by championing social justice, addressing wealth inequalities and pushing for poverty eradication.
“Thanks to the young people, the drive to foster societal improvement, demand for social justice, ending the inequities of wealth, and pushing for poverty eradication. These are paramount.
“A country can attract capital. It can acquire technology. It still needs people who know how to make that technology work and make it better,” said Anwar.
The prime minister arrived here on Tuesday for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou. — Bernama
8b0c3b2915d5930c: SEREMBAN: Calm returned to Balai Undang Luak Sungai Ujong here after Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar left the premises shortly after noon today.
Police personnel who had been stationed around the area also dispersed after the situation was brought under control.
Tunku Nadzaruddin and the four Undang, whose appointments are disputed, were seen leaving the balai in their respective official vehicles from about 12.15pm.
Earlier, more than 50 police personnel were deployed around Balai Undang Sungai Ujong near Ampangan, with several trucks also seen in the area.
Tunku Nadzaruddin and the four Undang were understood to have been inside the premises.
Media personnel who arrived at the location to cover the situation were not allowed to approach the building and were told to leave.

The development followed reports that a meeting between Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, the state executive council (Exco) members and Tunku Nadzaruddin, which was scheduled to be held at the Tuanku Ja'afar Royal Gallery here, had been cancelled on security grounds.
The Menteri Besar was later reported to have had breakfast with the exco members and several government backbenchers.
Reports also quoted lawyers representing Tunku Nadzaruddin and the four Undang as claiming that they were unable to leave Balai Undang Sungai Ujong due to a police blockade.
Attempts to reach the lawyers, Emirul Sarifudin Nor Azmi, for comment were unsuccessful.
Efforts to obtain comment from Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad on the claim were also unsuccessful.
f57dd352c5e3a0db: PUTRAJAYA: Mahkamah Rayuan menolak permohonan Rosmah Mansor mendapatkan penangguhan tanpa syarat terhadap perintah Mahkamah Tinggi yang memerintahkan pembayaran sekitar RM67.5 juta kepada syarikat barang kemas dari Lubnan sementara menunggu rayuannya.

Panel tiga hakim dipengerusikan Hakim Firuz Jaffril, berkata isteri bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak itu gagal mengemukakan alasan mencukupi bagi penangguhan tanpa syarat, sementara menunggu pelupusan rayuan yang dijadual didengar, pada 25 Mac tahun depan.
Panel hakim yang turut dianggotai Hakim Amarjeet Singh dan Aliza Sulaiman juga memerintahkan Rosmah membayar kos RM30,000.
"Datuk David, anda boleh melakukan apa sahaja yang anda mahu (untuk menguatkuasakan penghakiman Mahkamah Tinggi)," kata Firuz kepada peguam Global Royalty Trading SAL, David Gurupatham.

Pada 10 Jun, Hakim Mahkamah Tinggi Quay Chew Soon membenarkan saman Global Royalty terhadap Rosmah apabila memerintahkan pembayaran RM67.5 juta dalam tempoh sebulan, bagi 43 barang kemas yang didakwa dipinjamkan kepadanya.
Saman itu melibatkan 43 barang kemas mewah bernilai USD14.57 juta (sekitar RM67.5 juta) yang didakwa oleh Global Royalty dibekalkan kepada Rosmah pada 2018 secara konsainan untuk dilihat.
Syarikat tersebut mendakwa, barang kemas berkenaan kekal sebagai hak miliknya dan tidak pernah dikembalikan, lalu mendorongnya tuntutan ganti rugi daripada Rosmah.
Global Royalty, syarikat berpangkalan di Lubnan berkenaan turut menamakan ketua polis negara dan kerajaan sebagai defendan.

Pada 12 Ogos, Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman Marianne Antoinette Ghani membenarkan penangguhan bersyarat kepada Rosmah, yang menghendakinya memasukkan jumlah penuh penghakiman kira-kira RM67.5 juta ke akaun bersama yang dipegang peguam kedua pihak dalam tempoh sebulan.

Katanya, pengaturan tersebut akan melindungi hak Global Royalty terhadap wang berkenaan jika rayuan Rosmah gagal, sambil memastikan dana itu kekal di Malaysia dan boleh dikembalikan kepada Rosmah sekiranya beliau berjaya merayu.
Rosmah kemudian merayu kepada Mahkamah Rayuan untuk mendapatkan penangguhan tanpa syarat.

Peguamnya, Reza Abdul Rahim, hari ini, berhujah Mahkamah Rayuan mempunyai budi bicara membenarkan penangguhan sedemikian, terutamanya memandangkan rayuan terbabit dijadual didengar dalam tempoh kira-kira enam bulan.

Gurupatham yang dibantu R Venothani, membantah permohonan tersebut sambil berhujah Global Royalty akan dinafikan manfaat daripada penghakiman berkenaan susulan pembekuan aset Rosmah berkait saman difailkan 1MDB terhadapnya.
Beliau turut merujuk kepada afidavit Rosmah dengan menyatakan beliau mendakwa hanya mempunyai RM20 dalam akaun bank yang tidak aktif.
Peguam Kanan Persekutuan Siti Aishah Ramlan yang bertindak bagi pihak ketua polis negara dan kerajaan, berkata beliau mendapat arahan untuk tidak membantah permohonan Rosmah.
459a0725c3dddb4d: NAGOYA: Youth and Sports Minister Dr Taufiq Johari is confident the national contingent will achieve the six gold, seven silver and 20 bronze medal target that it has been given for the ongoing Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
Dr Taufiq said he was pleased with Malaysia's haul at the Games so far, which included a "bonus" gold from karate exponent Adeola Fay Robert (women's kumite under-55kg) on Tuesday.

"Our athletes have been training for a long time for this competition and now is the time for them to prove that they can win for Malaysia.
"I believe that other sports, not only karate, can also contribute 'bonus' medals for us."

Malaysia could win another karate gold later on Wednesday when C. Shahmalarani faces Hong Kong's Tsang Yee Ting in the women's under-50kg final.
ccefacfe8a4a5731: PETALING JAYA: A meeting between Negeri Sembilan menteri besar Ismail Lasim and his former executive council members with Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar has been cancelled.
Quoting a source, Sinar Harian said the meeting, which was scheduled to be held at 9am, was called off due to "security concerns".
It was reported yesterday that the meeting was intended to be an "ice-breaking" session and to build rapport between Tunku Nadzaruddin, Ismail and the former exco members.
The four purported undangs, Tunku Besar of Tampin, and Shahbandar of Sungai Ujong were also expected to attend.
The development comes amid a constitutional crisis in the state.

On Sept 17, the Attorney‑General’s Chambers (AGC) rejected a proclamation purporting to remove Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as state ruler, along with a subsequent announcement by the state executive council affirming it.
The AGC said the proclamation was invalid, and that the menteri besar and exco members had no unilateral power to remove the state ruler.

On Sept 20, Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of 10 executive council members, citing breaches of their oaths of office. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim was granted an audience with him the following day.
2c0b98b0242a0143: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The government expects the oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) sector to increase its output and revenue in the next two to three years through expansion into overseas markets, said Minister of Economy Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.

Speaking to reporters today, he said greater international market participation would strengthen the sector’s revenue streams while improving the resilience of Malaysian OGSE companies against economic and industry shocks.

“When we talk about the potential in terms of the international oil and gas market, developing countries will be a good place for us to venture into and that is why in terms of our planning through this international market access programme, Timor-Leste will be among the destinations that we will go into.

“But definitely the groundwork must be done through Malaysia Petroleum Resources Corporation (MPRC) to build up the rapport and provide the mechanism and really to ease the process,” said Akmal Nasrullah after the preview of MPRC International Market Access Programme’s (IMAP) Privet OGSE Turkmenistan here today.
Also present were Ministry of Economy secretary general, Datuk Seri Nor Azmie Diron and MPRC president/chief executive officer Mohd Yazid Ja’afar.
In 2023, the sector generated about RM79 billion in gross output and RM39.4 billion in value added to the economy.
As part of the effort, 14 Malaysian OGSE companies will participate in an upcoming mission to Turkmenistan in October to assess opportunities in the Central Asian country’s oil and gas industry.
Akmal Nasrullah said the companies were selected based on their capabilities, credibility and interest in exploring opportunities in Turkmenistan.

868e549a429031fb: CHIBA: The death toll from Typhoon Dujuan, which struck eastern Japan earlier this week, rose to nine on Wednesday after a woman was confirmed dead in Kanagawa Prefecture and a man was found in a submerged vehicle in Chiba prefecture, east of Tokyo.

020d657b1d896fc2: SINGAPORE: From pre-bleached straight hair wigs to wavy clipped extensions and blinged-out coffin-shaped nails, sales of Chinese-made beauty accessories are surging across the United States.

While friction over soaring Chinese exports of high-profile items such as cars and batteries forms the backdrop to this week's presidential summit, the boom in the non-strategic beauty sector underlines China's manufacturing prowess.

"This market is growing," said Joe Wu, an exporter in the central city of Xuchang, known as China's wig capital, who expects his sales to grow 40% this year, driven heavily by US buyers drawn through the apps TikTok and Instagram.
China's US exports of hair products rose 12.4% year-on-year to US$1.3 billion in the first half of 2026, customs data shows, with shipments on track to beat 2025's full-year figure of US$2.3 billion.
It is one of the fastest growing export categories alongside more conventional ones, such as computer parts, scooters or plastic goods.
While there is no customs data for artificial nails, which are categorised as plastic products, producers say business is booming.

Zhang Da, the owner of a 200-worker press-on nail factory in the eastern county of Donghai, says exports climbed to 70% of total revenue this year from 20% late in 2025, with US sales making up a large chunk.

The trend demonstrates that Beijing occupies "a unique historical position" in using scale and product upgrades to dominate global markets in both advanced and lower value-added goods, said Dan Wang, the China director of Eurasia Group.

"It is not just competing with the industrial products of one or two countries, it is competing with all industrial products globally," Wang said, a scenario that presented a problem for other countries, rather than China.
"It is going to be very difficult to see China's advantage replaced for many years to come."
Chinese exporters of beauty accessories have capitalised on the proliferation of influencers and celebrities on social media who frequently change wigs and manicures.

To do so, Chinese manufacturing centres have relied on labour forces that would be hard to replicate elsewhere — in Xuchang alone, for example, about 300,000 of a population of 4.4 million work in the hair industry, state media said.
Donghai, a county of 1 million people in the eastern city of Lianyungang, had nearly 25,000 press-on nail businesses.
Wu, in Xuchang, said its producers can outcompete rivals in places like Southeast Asia through efficiencies gained from large output capacity.
They mostly outsource the labour-intensive process of tying individual hair strands to laces used in wigs to North Korea, while sourcing some of the hair domestically from rural areas.
"The hair industry is just like any other sector - it relies on economies of scale, coupled with upstream and downstream supply chain integration," Wu added.
TIKTOK SALES

Hair products took 17 of the top 20 spots in TikTok sales revenue rankings for US fashion accessories in August, according to data analytics platform Fast Moss. The top-selling item was a glueless, pre-bleached straight-hair wig.
Ranked seventh was a men's bracelet with Bible verses, in 13th place was a hand-sized stitching device, and 20th was a pair of sunglasses.
Another hair product seller from Xuchang, who only gave his surname, Tian, said his US sales rose 10% to 15% over last year.
"Customers there really value personalisation," Tian said, citing a feature that lets him charge higher prices for lower volumes.
US clients account for a monthly revenue stream of US$10,000, said a TikTok livestreamer from a nail shop in Donghai who sought anonymity.
Producers are unfazed by any prospects of further US trade curbs, saying US demand is strong and supply cannot easily scale up outside China.
"Tariffs have an impact, but they are not the decisive factor," Wu added.

3f807fb659500647: The escalating constitutional crisis in Negeri Sembilan — triggered by the Undang Yang Empat’s attempt to depose the Yang Dipertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, and the resulting executive deadlock — demands a swift resolution rooted in the rule of law. Left unaddressed, any verdict risks rejection by opposing factions, threatening total administrative collapse.

To break the impasse and preserve public welfare, the federal government should advise the Yang di-Pertuan Agong to declare a localised state of emergency under Article 150 of the Federal Constitution.

This mechanism offers the cleanest path forward. Much like the 1977 Kelantan precedent under then prime minister, Hussein Onn, an emergency would freeze political manoeuvring, suspend the state constitution, and allow a neutral, non-political caretaker administrator to maintain governance.

Crucially, this intervention provides the stability needed for a definitive legal remedy. Under Article 34 of the Negeri Sembilan Constitution, the ruler can make a formal reference to the Federal Court for an authoritative opinion.

With the emergency preventing rival factions from sowing chaos, the apex court can dispassionately evaluate whether the Undangs adhered to due process and Adat Perpatih (customary law), and whether the subsequent dismissal of the state executive council holds legal weight.

Alternative pathways may fall short. Mediation by the Conference of Rulers or dissolving the state assembly to hold fresh elections might address political symptoms, but neither can decisively resolve the underlying royal dispute. Factional discontent among the Undangs would likely persist.
A full panel review by the Federal Court remains the only mechanism capable of delivering a legally binding, indisputable verdict.
By combining an immediate emergency declaration with an expedited apex court reference, Malaysia can safeguard institutional order and decisively restore the rule of law in Negeri Sembilan.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
c4db937f45a53c56: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — China Eastern Airlines plans to increase its Shanghai-Kota Kinabalu services to double or even triple daily flights, while exploring a direct Beijing-Kota Kinabalu route.

931ec199bb713a34: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Nine people were injured when a Health Ministry van overturned and landed on its driver’s side in an accident along Jalan Sultan Iskandar near Little India in Ipoh this morning.

2df608f3909fb8de: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal has refused Rosmah Mansor’s bid for an unconditional stay of a High Court order requiring her to pay about RM67.5 million to a Lebanese jewellery company pending her appeal.

A three-member bench chaired by Justice Firuz Jaffril said the wife of former prime minister Najib Razak did not advance sufficient grounds for an unconditional stay pending the disposal of the appeal, which is scheduled to be heard on March 25 next year.
The bench, which included Justices Amarjeet Singh and Aliza Sulaiman, also ordered Rosmah to pay RM30,000 in costs.
"Datuk David, you can do whatever you want (to enforce the High Court judgment)," Firuz told Global Royalty Trading SAL’s counsel, David Gurupatham.
On June 10, High Court judge Quay Chew Soon allowed Global Royalty’s suit against Rosmah, ordering her to pay RM67.5 million within a month for 43 pieces of jewellery allegedly loaned to her.
The suit concerned 43 pieces of luxury jewellery worth US$14.57 million (about RM67.5 million) which Global Royalty said it supplied to Rosmah in 2018 on consignment for viewing.
The company claimed the jewellery remained its property and was never returned, prompting it to seek compensation from Rosmah.
Global Royalty, a Lebanon-based company, also named the inspector-general of police and government as defendants.

On Aug 12, judicial commissioner Marianne Antoinette Ghani granted Rosmah a conditional stay, requiring her to place the full judgment sum of about RM67.5 million in a joint account held by the solicitors for both parties within one month.
She said the arrangement would safeguard Global Royalty’s right to the money if Rosmah’s appeal failed, while ensuring the funds remained in Malaysia and could be returned to Rosmah if she succeeded.
Rosmah then appealed to the Court of Appeal for an unconditional stay.
Her lawyer, Reza Abdul Rahim, today submitted that the appellate court had the discretion to grant such a stay, particularly as the appeal was due to be heard in about six months.

Gurupatham, assisted by R Venothani, opposed the application, saying Global Royalty would be deprived of the benefit of its judgment because Rosmah's assets had been frozen in connection with a suit filed by 1MDB against her.
He also referred to Rosmah's affidavit, saying she claimed to have only RM20 in a dormant bank account.
Senior federal counsel Siti Aishah Ramlan, appearing for the inspector-general of police and government, said she had instructions not to oppose Rosmah's application.
115fcb84e53944e3: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia aims to raise exports to account for 50 per cent of the oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) industry's revenue by 2030, as it pushes more local companies into overseas markets, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said.
Akmal said greater internationalisation was necessary to strengthen the resilience of the sector by diversifying its markets, customers and revenue streams.

The push is particularly important for smaller OGSE players, given that 91.6 per cent of the industry's 2,894 establishments were micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in 2023, he said at the launch of MPRC's International Market Access Programme (IMAP) Privet OGSE Turkmenistan here today.
"That's why this is an effort for us to really scale up their potentials, and this can be done also by looking at the opportunity for them to venture into the international market."

The export ambition forms part of the National OGSE Industry Blueprint 2021-2030, which calls for greater diversification, competitiveness, technology development and participation in international markets.
Akmal said the number of Malaysian companies that had ventured into overseas markets remained limited, particularly among listed companies, despite the size of the domestic OGSE industry.

The Department of Statistics Malaysia's inaugural OGSE Census recorded 2,894 establishments in 2023, generating RM79.2 billion in gross output and RM39.4 billion in value added, while employing more than 123,000 people.
He said the government was therefore seeking to help more OGSE companies scale up and move beyond reliance on the domestic market.

"We want to venture into it, even for our OGSE players, to look for opportunities in Turkmenistan. So definitely this is also part of preparation for our players to go for the international market and not just to rely on domestic or even on Petronas per se in Malaysia," he said.
As part of the push, 14 Malaysian OGSE companies will participate in a programme to Turkmenistan in October to assess potential business opportunities in the Central Asian market.
Akmal said Timor-Leste was also among the destinations being considered under IMAP, while other markets would be assessed based on their potential, risks and opportunities.

He said the government was targeting a more sustainable form of overseas participation, rather than one-off projects, with Malaysian companies expected to build recurring contracts, partnerships and an established presence where commercially viable.
He said the government's role was to create pathways and reduce barriers, while companies must convert those opportunities into commercially sustainable businesses.

Akmal added that Malaysian OGSE companies already had an advantage from decades of experience working with major international energy operators, giving them capabilities in engineering, fabrication, maintenance, marine services, digital solutions and specialised technical services.
He said the country's OGSE industry remained strategically relevant despite the energy transition, with gas expected to play an important role in ensuring stable energy supply.
The government, he said, would continue supporting the sector's internationalisation while also pursuing the National Energy Transition Roadmap and strengthening energy security.
"Resilience is not only about weathering shocks; it is about building more sources of growth before the next shock arrives," he said.
37dbe1314a01fe03: KUALA LUMPUR: Racing sim driver Taj Izrin Aiman Taj Madira saved his best for last to claim Malaysia's first Asian Games esports gold on Wednesday.

e232ee7b3cef6cbe: PARIS: Nations are not on track to meet a historic pledge to protect 30% of the world's land and oceans by 2030, a new study said Wednesday.
The findings follow a similar assessment by the UN and come ahead of a global summit in Armenia where nations will review progress toward the biodiversity targets.
The "30x30" goal was the centrepiece of a landmark pact reached in 2022 by nearly 200 nations that was informally dubbed the "Paris Agreement for nature".
But rhetoric had not been followed by action, said a report by environmental groups Campaign for Nature and Together for the Ocean.
"Governments have already demonstrated that rapid progress is possible, but the world is not yet on track to achieve 30% coverage," Campaign for Nature director Brian O'Donnell told reporters.
If governments delivered their commitments in full, the amount of land and inland waters designated as protected or conserved could reach 27% by 2030, the report said.
But oceans might only reach 12% coverage by the end of the decade.
In a statement last month, the Convention on Biological Diversity, the UN treaty that oversees the global nature goals, also warned that countries were off track.
Money for conservation is one of the biggest barriers.
The report's authors estimated that between US$100 billion and US$180 billion was needed every year to reach the 2030 target – but annual spending lagged at roughly US$24 billion.
"The gap is particularly stark for the ocean, where approximately US$16 billion is needed annually but only an estimated US$1.8 billion is currently spent," the report said.
Much of the funding would be needed in developing countries, which host many of the world's richest ecosystems but lack the means to properly defend these biodiversity hotspots.

O'Donnell said governments would need to dig deeper into their budgets but could also legislate to require that polluting industries – such as fossil fuel and mining companies – contribute to conservation.
"They're not going to do that voluntarily," he said.
He said the 30x30 goal "remains achievable" but not without a big lift.
"We don't want to sugarcoat this and say this will not be without a challenge," he said.
The biodiversity pact committed nations to halting and reversing nature loss by 2030, including by meeting the 30x30 target, cutting pollution and restoring ecosystems.
The UN biodiversity summit in Yerevan, starting Oct 19, is the first time nations will address the progress shortfall and discuss how to get the targets back on track.
62c1e8c39bb460d8: KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities are carrying out a detailed assessment of the structural safety of an apartment block in Bandar Damai Perdana, Cheras, after a landslide forced about 80 residents to evacuate last night.

39aba1760c212eda: LOS ANGELES:] Polls opened Tuesday in the only American election that really matters: Fat Bear Week.

While the United States might be gearing up for midterm ballots that will decide who runs Washington, hundreds of thousands of people were readying to vote on animals gorging themselves in rural Alaska.

In a contest that has rapidly become one of the internet's favourite moments, the brown bears of Katmai National Park unwittingly compete in a series of head-to-head contests to see which one of them has most impressively piled on the pounds ahead of hibernation.

Viewers can watch a livestream of the enormous animals as they scoop salmon from the Brooks River, or browse biographies of some of the top contenders, including before-and-after pictures showing how much weight the bears have gained over a summer of feasting.
"For each match-up, vote for the bear you believe best exemplifies fatness and success in brown bears," said organisers.
"The bear with the most votes advances to the next round. Only one will be crowned Fat Bear Week champion."
Last year's winner, Chunk, beat out a stiff challenge from two-time winner Grazer.
Summer and early autumn are key fueling periods for the brown bears, which will not eat for five months of hibernation, relying on their store of fat to survive the punishing Alaskan winter.

The online contest began in 2014 with just a few thousand people voting, but has now turned into an eagerly awaited exercise in tongue-in-cheek democracy with more than a million people voting every year.
The aim is to raise awareness of brown bears and their habitat in Alaska, and the risks they face from human activity.
52314215237fd537: KUALA LUMPUR: AME Real Estate Investment Trust (AME Reit) is expected to see stronger earnings in financial year 2027 (FY27), driven by rental reversions at Senai Airport City (SAC) and Indahpura, alongside initial contributions from the i-Park SAC 34 acquisition.

While general portfolio guidance points to renewal rental reversions of about 11 to 13 per cent (capped at around 20 per cent), Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said AME Reit's recent track record suggests stronger potential in SAC.
It noted that SAC's passing rents of RM1.85 to RM1.90 per square foot (psf) remained more than 35 per cent below current market rates of above RM2.50 psf.

"Management's track record in securing about 40 per cent reversions recently on replacement tenants confirms the prevalence of this market gap, signalling significant organic upside for upcoming lease expirations in the segment.

"Top-line growth in FY27 will be further underpinned by a nine-month inorganic revenue contribution from the i-Park SAC 34 acquisition (completed June 30, 2026), which also enjoys a built-in 3 per cent annual step-up through FY30," it said.

Given Indahpura's deeper discount to SAC market rates, it said rental reversions have been noticeably stronger.

"A recent renewal with an existing tenant achieved a rental uplift of more than 30 per cent, exceeding comparable SAC renewals of 11 to 20 per cent and narrowing the rental gap to about 10 sen to 15 sen psf.
