Overall, HLIB said defensive master-leased dormitories safeguard baseline yields, leaving the i-Park @ SAC build-to-lease project to unlock the next earnings inflection from FY29.
"Following our coverage resumption, we introduce our FY27 to FY29 earnings forecasts. We maintain a "Buy" recommendation on AME Reit with a target price of RM1.67," it added.

36dc6a0d7cd8ae93: KUALA LUMPUR: Eco World Development Group Bhd's (EcoWorld) RM1.013 billion land sale to Tera Data Centers (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd is expected to provide a positive boost to its sales and earnings, said CGS International Research.

920315811213b934: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — A scheduled meeting between Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, state executive councillors and Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar was cancelled this morning due to safety considerations.

5ff4b457316d7db2: SHAH ALAM: Confusion over the angle of closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage led to speculation linking a police mobile patrol vehicle (MPV) to a cable theft syndicate in Kampung Tasek Tambahan, Ampang, on Sept 18.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the MPV policemen were carrying out official duties after receiving information about the incident, and were not protecting the suspected criminals.
"I have checked the matter and there is actually no controversy. The MPV policemen who conducted the patrol were carrying out their duties.
"However, I noticed that the issue arose from the angles of the footage, which appeared to create controversy," he said at a press conference at the Selangor police headquarters here today.
On the chronology of the incident, Shazeli said police rushed to the location after receiving a report about cable theft to verify the information.
He said the personnel who arrived at the scene did not initially expect a large number of suspects to be in the area.
"Although several suspects fled after realising the presence of the authorities, police managed to arrest one person at the scene.
"We have arrested one suspect and investigations are ongoing. The suspect was charged under Section 379 of the Penal Code and fined RM8,000," he said.
Shazeli said police were now actively tracking down the remaining accomplices who were still at large.
"Further investigations are being conducted to establish the authenticity of the footage and determine whether there were any weaknesses in relation to the incident.

"Sharing the video is not an issue. Police welcome the sharing of information. However, my advice is not to jump to conclusions before the full story is known, as this could lead to false accusations," he said.
Earlier, CCTV footage recorded by a house near the scene went viral on several social media platforms, including Facebook and Threads.
The footage drew various reactions from netizens, including claims that the police vehicle was escorting a vehicle believed to be carrying stolen cables.
5a11213357071e26: PETALING JAYA: Seorang bekas Ahli Parlimen berkata Belanjawan 2027 perlu menangani isu gaji rendah di Malaysia serta hakikat bahawa rakyat masih belum menikmati manfaat daripada pertumbuhan ekonomi.
Memetik kajian pusat penyelidikan bebas Khazanah Research Institute, Charles Santiago dari DAP berkata 70% rakyat Malaysia tidak merasai kesan pertumbuhan ekonomi.

Beliau turut merujuk data Jabatan Perangkaan yang menunjukkan dua daripada tiga penerima upah di Malaysia bekerja dalam pekerjaan separa mahir atau berkemahiran rendah, dengan gaji median masing-masing hanya RM2,223 dan RM1,758.

Santiago berkata walaupun Keluaran Dalam Negara Kasar (KDNK), pendapatan negara kasar dan pelaburan langsung asing Malaysia meningkat, rakyat tidak akan menikmati kemakmuran sekiranya pertumbuhan gaji gagal mengimbangi kos sara hidup.
“Ekonomi mungkin berkembang, tetapi keadaan kewangan isi rumah mereka tidak semestinya bertambah baik.

“Inilah persoalan yang mesti dijawab Belanjawan 2027: Bilakah pertumbuhan ekonomi akhirnya akan diterjemahkan kepada pendapatan isi rumah dan jaminan kewangan yang lebih kukuh?” kata Santiago, yang pernah menjadi Ahli Parlimen Klang selama tiga penggal, dalam hantaran di X.

Beliau turut menggesa kerajaan memperkenalkan strategi gaji yang serius, memperkukuh perlindungan sosial dan mengambil tindakan terhadap kos sara hidup, 'bukan satu lagi langkah atau satu kali pengumuman sahaja'.
Katanya, negara perlu “berhenti berpura-pura” bahawa bantuan tunai sekali beri mampu menyelesaikan krisis kemampuan hidup yang bersifat struktur.
“9 Okt harus menjadi hari untuk meletakkan kemakmuran isi rumah sebagai teras dasar ekonomi,” katanya, merujuk kepada tarikh pembentangan belanjawan negara.
Pada 23 Ogos, Menteri Komunikasi merangkap jurucakap kerajaan, Fahmi Fadzil, berkata Belanjawan 2027 akan mengutamakan langkah untuk mengurangkan tekanan akibat peningkatan kos sara hidup.
Fahmi berkata penyediaan belanjawan itu akan mengambil kira pelbagai faktor, termasuk harga minyak mentah dunia.
adcee54eddeb8e9c: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Malaysia underscored its regional leadership in skills development and green workforce readiness at the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 Conference, reaffirming its long-standing commitment to elevating technical and vocational excellence.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim highlighted the country’s newly entrusted role to lead the regional green jobs agenda following the Asean Plus Three Labour Ministers Meeting in Bangkok.

“Malaysia was entrusted to lead the Regional Green Jobs Agenda for 2026 to 2030, which will help prepare our workforces for greener economies,” he said during his special address at the conference and expo’s opening plenary at the National Exhibition and Convention Centre.
“We have also championed cross-border recognition of technical certificates and piloted an Asean Digital Skills Passport that links certified training records across the region,” he said.

Anwar, who is also the finance minister, cited Malaysia’s National Semiconductor Strategy, under which an investment target of over RM500 billion by 2030 was set, while it also aimed to train and upskill 60,000 highly skilled Malaysian engineers.
“Investment arrives in Malaysia for many reasons. But we all know that it principally grows where there are enough skills to nourish it,” he added.

About 1,400 skilled young people from over 65 countries and regions are gathering in China’s largest city to compete across 64 skill categories. Malaysia has sent 22 young competitors across 21 skill areas.
The Prime Minister arrived here on Tuesday for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou.
In the afternoon, the Prime Minister and his delegation will travel by high-speed train to Hangzhou, the capital of Zhejiang province, for the second leg of the visit.

Upon arrival, Anwar is slated to hold one-on-one business meetings with tech giants AgiBot, Huawei and Alibaba Group, as well as automotive company Geely and Chinese multinational technology and telecommunications equipment company ZTE Group.
Anwar will later attend a welcoming dinner hosted by Chinese Premier Li Qiang.
The Prime Minister is also scheduled to launch a book titled “Rethinking Ourselves: Justice, Reform, and Ignorance in Post Normal Times”, which has been translated into Mandarin.
China remains Malaysia’s largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, with total bilateral trade reaching US$113.82 billion (RM456.68 billion) from January to August this year. — Bernama
4e9ce00417b2daae: KUALA LUMPUR: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said that any decision on the Negri Sembilan debacle must be anchored in the state's own foundational law, the Negri Sembilan Constitution.
"I want to stress just one thing here. I think we have to go back to the Undang-Undang Tubuh Negeri (state constitution), because that is the state constitution.

"I do not want to take sides - who is right, who is wrong - but for me, any decision on anything, you have to go back to the main law, which is the Undang-Undang Tubuh," she told reporters after attending the Anti-Bullying Act 2026 Literacy Programme and the Role of the Anti-Bullying Tribunal (TAB) at the Royal Military College (RMC).

Azalina, who is also Pengerang member of parliament, said she lacked the expertise to pronounce on the intricacies of Adat Pepatih, the matrilineal customary system that underpins Negri Sembilan's constitutional arrangements.

"Negri Sembilan is a bit unique compared to other states. If we want to comment and we are not from Negri Sembilan, I think it is also a bit unfair. I am confident that the people of Negri Sembilan should be the ones to find the solution.
"But that is my personal view, not the view of the Legal Affairs Division. I am a Johor person," she added.

Asked about the Attorney-General's Chambers' (A-GC) statement that the state executive council had no authority to suspend the duties of the state secretary and state legal adviser, Azalina said she had no involvement in any such decision and could not comment beyond what was publicly available.
She highlighted her personal opinion, however, that changing a state secretary was not unusual when a new menteri besar took office, and pointed to precedents at both the federal and state levels.

"When Tun Mahathir was prime minister, he changed the attorney-general. When Tan Sri Muhyiddin became prime minister, that too was a norm of leadership. Even Selangor changed its state secretary when a new menteri besar came in.
"But to comment further on the A-GC's statement, I do not have enough information. I read the same things everyone else reads," she said.

On the call by 10 former presidents of the Malaysian Bar for the federal government to step in and resolve the constitutional issues in the state, Azalina said the boundaries between state and federal jurisdiction had to be respected.
She said the federal government could not simply step into matters that were constitutionally the state's preserve.
"We must respect the state - it has its own laws, its own constitution.
"The federal government has ours. These are different things," she said, adding that she would not risk misleading the public on matters outside her expertise.
She said Negri Sembilan's elected representatives in the federal cabinet were better placed to address the state-specific dimensions of the crisis.
Yesterday, the A-GC said the Negri Sembilan state executive council had no legal authority to suspend the state secretary and state legal adviser.

The A-GC said matters relating to the appointment, including the suspension of the two office-holders, fall under the jurisdiction of the Public Service Commission and the Judicial and Legal Service Commission.
It said this was provided for under Article 37 of the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959.
This was after Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim announced the suspension of state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal with immediate effect.

e0828dbba51ceb01: MUMBAI, Sept 23 — In little over a month, the chairman of India’s corporate giant Tata Group has gone from seeking another term to announcing his departure to returning to the role.
The saga around N. Chandrasekaran, who has headed the multi-billion-dollar empire for nearly a decade, has laid bare the succession challenge confronting India’s industrial behemoths.

The leadership battle at Tata Group, whose businesses span everything from Jaguar Land Rover cars to Apple iPhone assembly, has highlighted weaknesses in governance and the power struggle between boards and controlling families.
But the consequences extend far beyond shareholders, with a growing number of succession dramas shaking global confidence in India, whose economy relies heavily on corporate giants, analysts say.
The Tata fiasco came to a head last week when the board of Tata Sons, the group’s holding company, granted Chandrasekaran another five-year term.
The announcement came despite objections from the Tata Trusts, the philanthropic entities that control the conglomerate and which is chaired by family patriarch Noel Tata.
“The mutiny of the board against the controlling shareholder is possibly a first, and not the right precedent for corporate India,” independent advisory firm IiAS said in a note.
Tata is far from an isolated case: from banks to consumer goods, some of India’s biggest companies have been rocked by leadership exits and botched handovers in recent months.
“In the last 18-24 months, we’ve seen a number of CEOs being churned at the top,” Navnit Singh of executive search firm Korn Ferry told AFP.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

This file picture shows Tata Sons chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran (right) and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Tata Passenger Electric Mobility managing director Shailesh Chandra posing with the ‘Avinya’ concept car during its unveiling in Mumbai on April 29, 2022.
“I do think boards may not be spending enough time looking at long-term succession. Often enough companies do not have a ‘hit by the bus’ contingent plan and are often caught off guard.”
The roots of the Tata conflict run deep.
For much of the year, Chandrasekaran’s future hung in the balance as Noel Tata raised concerns about losses at some group companies, investment spending and the possibility of listing Tata Sons.
Leadership crisis
The tensions intensified after the death of former patriarch Ratan Tata in 2024, leaving unresolved questions over how authority would be shared within India’s largest conglomerate.
“When Ratan was alive, he didn’t trust Noel Tata enough to make him the chairman of the Trusts,” said Shriram Subramanian of advisory firm InGovern.
“He didn’t ensure that there was a structured handover of power even when he was alive.”
A succession crisis has also rocked India’s largest private lender, HDFC Bank.

The bank’s chief executive Sashidhar Jagdishan declined another term last month, an abrupt departure that came after the shock resignation of its chairman, forcing directors into a hurried search for new leadership.

At Godrej Consumer Products, chief executive Sudhir Sitapati secured shareholder approval for a second five-year term in August only to resign days later, fuelling speculation about tensions between management and the founding Godrej family.
Experts say such episodes reveal a failure by boards to prepare for leadership transitions before they become crises.

“Independent directors are meant to ask the uncomfortable question, ‘who’s next, and are they ready?’ years before it becomes urgent,” said Tulsi Jayakumar, an economics professor specialising in family business.
“Instead, most boards wait for a health scare or a boardroom crisis to even put succession on the agenda. That’s not governance, that’s crisis management wearing a governance hat.”
Ageing billionaires

The Tata Group’s annual revenues are roughly equivalent to about five per cent of India’s GDP, and it has become a key investor in strategic sectors including semiconductors, batteries and electronics manufacturing.
“When succession stumbles at a group the size of Tata, it isn’t a private family matter, it’s a systemic one,” Jayakumar said.
Such conglomerates sit at the centre of supply chains, employ hundreds of thousands of people and play an outsized role in shaping investor confidence, she noted.
“A prolonged succession fight signals to global capital that governance in India still runs on personality, not process,” she said.
The issue is particularly significant in a country where family-controlled businesses account for most economic activity.

India’s ageing billionaires are preparing for one of the biggest intergenerational transfers of wealth globally to their children — US$382 billion according to UBS data — which implies a massive shake-up in the way many of these empires will be run.
That transition could reshape some of the country’s biggest corporate empires and test whether boards are prepared to manage increasingly complex successions.

“Succession planning is under far greater public scrutiny now,” said Amit Tandon of IiAS, noting that investors understand that “when the baton is passed to the next generation... it changes the trajectory of the company”.
“The best way to look at it is that succession planning is an art, not a science,” he added.
“And Indian businesses haven’t really cracked it yet.” — AFP
ea7e20d5710d6cd7: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia placed two swimmers in the final for the first time in the Asian Games men's 200m freestyle at the Tokyo Aquatic Centre on Wednesday through Khiew Hoe Yean and Arvin Shaun Singh Chahal.

5f11cfab0459da09: PETALING JAYA: A former MP today said that the 2027 budget should respond to Malaysia's low wages and the fact that Malaysians are not experiencing the benefits of economic growth.
Citing a study by independent research centre Khazanah Research Institute, DAP’s Charles Santiago said 70% of Malaysians were not feeling the effects of economic growth.

He also referred to numbers from the statistics department which revealed that two in three Malaysian wage earners work in semi- or low-skilled occupations, with median wages of just RM2,223 and RM1,758.

Even if Malaysia's gross domestic product, gross national income and foreign direct investment increased, Santiago said the public would not experience prosperity if wages failed to keep up with the cost of living.
"The economy may be growing. Their household isn't necessarily getting better.

"This is the question that Budget 2027 must answer: when will economic growth finally translate into stronger household incomes and security?" Santiago, who was Klang MP for three terms, said in a post on X.
He also called for a serious wage strategy, stronger social protection and action on the cost of living, "not another one-off measure or announcement".
He said the country should "stop pretending" that one-off cash assistance could solve a structural affordability crisis.
"Oct 9 should be about putting household prosperity at the centre of economic policy," he said, referring to the date when the national budget will be tabled.
On Aug 23, communications minister and government spokesman Fahmi Fadzil said that Budget 2027 would prioritise measures to ease rising living costs.
Fahmi said the budget's preparation would take into account various factors, including global crude oil prices.
88a5f7b9bd3d97a6: GAZA CITY: In her Gaza City apartment, Heba Arafat walks uphill across a living room slanted at a steep angle after Israeli airstrikes caused the building's foundations to collapse, leaving the entire structure tilted.

Like thousands of people in Gaza, Arafat chose to risk living in an apartment building damaged during nearly three years of war between Israel and Hamas, with countless Israeli airstrikes on the Palestinian territory.
"We were forced to live here because we had nowhere else to go. All of our homes were destroyed, our land was razed, and we have nothing left," said Arafat, 47.
According to the UN, 84% of all structures in Gaza had been damaged or destroyed by October 2025, and Gaza's civil defence says 2,000 buildings across the territory are at risk of collapse.

Last week, 21 people, including 12 children, died in Gaza City after a six-storey building that local authorities said had been hit repeatedly by Israeli airstrikes collapsed. Israel denied having struck the building.

Arafat lives with her six daughters and husband in their old apartment building in Gaza City's Al-Shati Refugee Camp, which they left at the height of the war that began in October 2023 with Hamas's massive attack on Israel.

The family returned after an October 2025 ceasefire, which has reduced but not ended Israeli strikes. They found that their four-storey building, in which 30 people now live, had collapsed inward at the ground floor, the result, she said, of an Israeli ground operation in the area.
Like most buildings in Gaza City, the windows were blown away by blasts, with makeshift bedsheets spread across the frames providing little privacy.
As she spoke, Arafat illustrated her building's slant by leaving a water bottle sideways on the floor, only for it to quickly roll away to the other end of the room.

While no territory-wide estimate exists, Ramiz Alakbarov, the UN humanitarian coordinator for the Palestinian territories, said last week that people across Gaza were living in "hundreds of damaged and unsafe shelters".
'Where can we go?'
"Where can we go? Even though this house is dangerous," Arafat said. "We have been terrified ever since we heard about houses collapsing. The danger has become even greater than we thought."
Gaza City municipal staff patrol the streets to identify buildings at risk of collapse and mark them with stencils.

"These homes pose a genuine threat to the lives of the displaced persons sheltering inside them, as well as to residents in the vicinity and those in nearby displacement camps," said Hosni Muhanna, a Gaza City spokesman.
But Muhanna knows that people are likely to remain in these buildings for lack of better options.

"Thousands of displaced people are forced to seek shelter in these dilapidated buildings which are on the verge of collapse to escape the hardships of displacement camps that offer no protection against the summer heat or winter cold."

Most residents of Gaza were displaced at least once during the war, and many of them remain in enormous camps for the displaced, in tents provided by humanitarian organisations or in improvised shelters.
Stalled reconstruction

With diseases such as the skin infection impetigo rampaging through certain camps due to the lack of waste disposal and general overcrowding, many Gaza residents have found it safer to take the risks of moving into the damaged buildings.
And with Gaza's economy in tatters, many remain dependent on aid, which Israel has allowed into Gaza with restrictions since the declaration of the US-brokered ceasefire in October 2025.

But Israel has kept carrying out airstrikes and has restricted the entry of a range of equipment that it says could also have military use but which Gazans and international NGOs say are needed for the territory's vast reconstruction needs.

These can include large machinery needed to clear rubble from the site of destroyed buildings or spare parts and lubricants needed to keep other tools running, UN spokesman Stephane Dujarric said in August.
With the ceasefire process stalled for months, reconstruction efforts planned under the ceasefire have yet to begin.
According to a joint assessment published by the UN, World Bank and EU in April, Gaza will require US$71.4 billion in recovery and reconstruction spending over the next decade.
"We're afraid a wall or the roof might fall on us, so we huddle together, afraid that one of us might get hurt," Arafat said.
92d0b7f103f7ad4c: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Malaysia is positioning Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) at the centre of its industrial policy, making it a key instrument of economic transformation to build a highly skilled and well-paid workforce.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the strategy forms a core part of the nation’s push to transition to a high-growth, high-value economy as it expands into chip design, artificial intelligence (AI), green technology and agri-food.

He said the ‘TVET 2.0’ reform phase aims to promote closer collaboration between industry players and training institutions while accelerating exposure to emerging fields such as semiconductors, AI and renewable energy.

Coordination of the national agenda is managed by the National TVET Council across around 1,400 institutions, involving 12 ministries, state governments and private providers, under the National TVET Policy 2030, he said.
“Companies know what equipment they use and how quickly their needs change. They should be partners in shaping talent from the outset and ensure they are ahead of the curve.
“A modern economy cannot function without the technicians who keep a semiconductor line running or an electric vehicle plant on schedule. The machinery may become more sophisticated.

“The software may become more intelligent. But somebody still has to understand how it works and know what to do when it does not,” said the Prime Minister in his 10-minute keynote address at the plenary session of the WorldSkills Conference 2026 here on Wednesday.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang officially opened the three-day conference, which carried the theme “Shaping a Skills-Driven Future”, at the National Exhibition and Convention Centre (NECC).

Held in parallel with the 48th WorldSkills Competition Shanghai 2026 and WorldSkills Expo, the conference brought together policymakers, educators, industry leaders and other stakeholders to discuss ways to strengthen global TVET systems.

Thanking the Chinese premier for the invitation to visit and the warm welcome extended to the Malaysian delegation, Anwar said Shanghai had changed immensely, evolving from its ‘mother industry’ of textile mills to become a hub for semiconductors and artificial intelligence.
“Every new industry has to be learned before it can be built. Malaysia has reached the same conclusion,” he said.

Anwar said Malaysia had set two major targets for 2030 under its National Semiconductor Strategy: securing RM500 billion in semiconductor investment and training or upskilling 60,000 highly skilled Malaysian engineers.

By leveraging China’s capabilities in advanced manufacturing, AI, robotics, industrial automation, electric vehicles, semiconductors and digital technologies, Malaysia seeks to strengthen TVET cooperation with China, he said.

“In TVET, we look forward to more exchanges between our students and instructors, more joint training programmes, closer links among TVET institutions and between institutions and industry, and wider sharing of technology and expertise.

“The Malaysia-China Youth TVET Training initiative already shows what cooperation between our institutions can achieve. I believe TVET can become one of the pillars of the wider relationship between Malaysia and China,” said Anwar. — Bernama
c495da5d939e9a4f: NEW YORK: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado made three unsuccessful bids to return to Venezuela in recent hours, her team and media said on Tuesday, as interim President Delcy Rodriguez met US President Donald Trump in New York.

The flurry of activity comes amid high-stakes diplomacy at the United Nations General Assembly, where Trump held his first meeting with Rodriguez since US forces captured then-President Nicolas Maduro during a raid in January.

Machado adviser Pedro Urruchurtu said on social media the latest sea and air attempts were among seven failed efforts to return since she clandestinely left Venezuela nine months ago, as reported by Spanish newspaper ABC.
The remarks were later confirmed by a spokesperson for Machado, who has not publicly commented on the failed attempts.
The US State Department did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
Following the June earthquakes in Venezuela, US officials privately urged Machado to postpone her return and opposed her efforts to re-enter the country, people familiar with the matter said.
Machado, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate, has been in exile since late last year following a period in hiding after the contested 2024 election.
Her arrival remains a point of contention, despite having repeatedly vowed to return after Maduro's ouster and two major earthquakes.
Newspaper ABC did not give details on who blocked the attempts by sea and air.

fbcb5bbcf3633c03: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The defamation suit filed by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim against Pendang Member of Parliament Datuk Awang Solahuddin Hashim was settled amicably at the High Court here today.
Anwar’s lawyer, Datuk SN Nair, informed Judge Roslan Mat Nor that both parties had reached an agreement on the terms of settlement.
“Both parties wish to record the agreed terms. Accordingly, the plaintiff withdraws the suit with no order as to costs and without liberty to file afresh.

“Both parties have attached a copy of a mutually agreed public statement to the consent motion. We thank the court and learned counsel, and request that the scheduled trial dates be vacated,” he said.
Meanwhile, lawyer Yusfarizal Yussoff, representing Awang Solahuddin, confirmed the matter.
Judge Roslan subsequently struck out the lawsuit with no order as to costs and without liberty to refile, while vacating the trial dates scheduled for October 26 to 29, 2026.
The judge expressed appreciation to Anwar and Awang Solahuddin for resolving the matter amicably and for Anwar’s decision to withdraw the case.

According to a public statement obtained by the media, the parties said they had reached a final settlement after considering the implications and costs of continuing the defamation proceedings, as well as the need to prioritise matters of greater importance to the people and the nation.

Under the terms of the settlement, Awang Solahuddin humbly and unequivocally withdrew all statements he made on or around Feb 21, 2023, which formed the basis of the legal action, and agreed not to repeat or republish any such statements, or statements conveying a similar meaning, in the future.
Both parties also expressed their utmost appreciation to the judge and court officials involved for their professionalism, wisdom, and efficiency throughout the proceedings.
They also urged all parties to respect the resolution and refrain from using the case to undermine national harmony, unity, and stability.
Anwar filed the suit on March 3, 2023, over statements allegedly made by Awang Solahuddin in the Parliament lobby while attending a Dewan Rakyat sitting on Feb 21, 2023.

The statements, which were recorded and made public, allegedly implied that Anwar had abused his powers as Prime Minister and Finance Minister by interfering with, obstructing, or issuing arbitrary directives to law-enforcement and prosecution agencies for personal political purposes.
Anwar maintained that the remarks damaged his reputation as a respected national and international leader. — Bernama

a635cd408c91993d: PHNOM PENH: Cambodia’s prime minister said the country would not be a haven for transnational scam syndicates as he opened a global conference on cyberfraud on Wednesday, where the government is keen to showcase its crackdown on the multibillion-dollar scam industry.

"Cambodia will never be a safe haven for online scams," Prime Minister Hun Manet said in an opening speech in Phnom Penh, where delegates from more than a dozen countries, including the United States and China, have gathered.

"Cambodia will not allow criminal syndicates to undermine our country's progress and the livelihood of over 17 million Cambodian people," he said, adding that the country supported more international cooperation including real-time intelligence sharing.
Cambodian authorities say they have eradicated industrial-scale scam compounds, a claim met with skepticism by some analysts who say raids have left high level figures unscathed.
The conference represents a "growing openness to cooperate", said Delphine Schantz, regional representative of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime.

“But it is clear that more can and needs to be done, both at national levels, and in terms of international cooperation,” she said, calling for a joint understanding of key trends and coherent regulatory frameworks including investment in digital evidence collection.

The country, along with other Southeast Asian nations, emerged in recent years as a hub for the transnational cyberscam industry, with mostly Chinese-led criminal gangs operating compounds where trafficking victims are detained and coerced into carrying out romance scams, police-impersonation fraud and other schemes.

On Monday and Tuesday, reporters toured sprawling centres shuttered by the government – one housing as many as 20,000 workers. They also viewed materials seized by police, including fake FBI and Chinese police badges used in impersonation schemes.

Under pressure from countries including the US, which estimates that Americans lost more than US$10 billion to scammers operating in the region in 2024 alone, Cambodia says it has raided hundreds of compounds and deported hundreds of thousands of people over the past year.

But analysts and opposition figures say the raids have left politically connected figures who allegedly protected the networks untouched, while criminal groups have adapted by breaking into smaller units and moving operations overseas.

The credibility of the crackdown “will depend on whether the Cambodian state is willing to investigate all credible allegations, regardless of wealth, influence or official position," Mu Sochua, an exiled opposition politician, said in a statement.
5ab827db55cac375: KUALA LUMPUR: Mahkamah Tinggi menolak permohonan semakan kehakiman badan pemantau alam sekitar, RimbaWatch terhadap dua kementerian berhubung dakwaan kegagalan mereka menyiasat aduan mengenai pengiklanan bahan api fosil yang 'mengelirukan'.
Permohonan itu bertujuan mencabar keputusan yang dibuat oleh Kementerian Sumber Asli dan Kelestarian Alam (NRES) serta Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup (KPDN) pada tahun lalu.
Peguam RimbaWatch, Kumaresan Thurairaju, berkata pesuruhjaya kehakiman Azizan Md Arshad menolak permohonan itu dalam kamar.
Mahkamah tidak membuat sebarang perintah berhubung kos.
Kumaresan berkata RimbaWatch akan merayu keputusan itu dan menulis surat kepada mahkamah untuk memohon alasan penghakimannya.
Peguam Kanan Persekutuan Syahriah Shapiee dan Intan Syafinaz Ros’lin hadir bagi pihak kedua-dua kementerian, manakala peguam Abhilaash Subramaniam hadir sebagai amicus curiae bagi Majlis Peguam.

Tahun lalu, RimbaWatch mengemukakan aduan kepada dua kementerian itu berhubung pemasaran sebuah syarikat bahan api fosil yang mendakwa produknya berasaskan bahan api fosil sebagai 'neutral karbon', dakwaan dianggap mengelirukan.

RimbaWatch berkata mereka mengemukakan aduan kepada dua kementerian itu kerana KPDN mewakili agensi di bawah menteri yang dilantik untuk melindungi pengguna, manakala NRES mewakili agensi di bawah menteri yang dilantik untuk mencegah pencemaran dan melindungi alam sekitar.
“Kami berpendapat jika dakwaan ini benar-benar mengelirukan seperti yang kami percaya, ia boleh menjejaskan kepentingan perlindungan pengguna dan iklim,” katanya dalam kenyataan.
Bagaimanapun, KPDN memaklumkan kepada RimbaWatch bahawa aduan itu di luar bidang kuasanya dan perlu dikemukakan kepada NRES.
NRES pula meminta RimbaWatch mengemukakan aduan itu kepada KPDN.
ab793330a8302f6c: SAO PAULO: Brazilian planemaker Embraer said on Tuesday it has been notified of reports of GPS system instability affecting certain aircraft types, including its E2 family.

Embraer said it was closely monitoring the situation in coordination with operators and the equipment manufacturer, while providing technical support to customers and taking the necessary steps to address the issue.
While the occurrence may affect airlines' operational schedules, there is no impact on flight safety, the planemaker added in a statement.
"The global E2 fleet is equipped with navigation systems and procedures that allow the aircraft to operate even under conditions of GPS system instability," Embraer said.

Honeywell Aerospace, whose equipment is fitted on affected aircraft, said it was aware of an issue affecting aircraft globally relating to the reception of GPS signals, and that its teams were "actively assessing the matter" to identify the underlying cause.
Brazilian carrier Azul said in a separate statement that instability has impacted the operation of its E2 fleet.
Azul said it was implementing operational measures that may result in adjustments to its route network and the schedules of certain flights.
Flight-tracking service Flightradar24 said on Wednesday that Azul's E2 aircraft were returning to flight.

876334d09e478de2: MADRID, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez yesterday blamed a failure of Moroccan border controls for a recent migrant crisis in Spain’s North African territory of Ceuta.
More than 70,000 migrants entered Ceuta on July 30 and 31 in an unprecedented and deadly rush.

Most returned to Morocco in the following hours. Several thousand, however, have remained in the Spanish enclave, where the situation has since deteriorated, leading to episodes of violence and almost daily demonstrations by local residents.

“We are investigating what happened in those days back in July but at the same time we have asked Morocco for actions and also for answers because it is also clear that its border control failed,” Sanchez said in English during an interview with CNN in New York.

Speaking in parliament on September 3, Sanchez said Madrid needed to ask the Moroccan authorities for “explanations and changes” to avoid a repeat of the migrant influx into Ceuta, while stressing there was no “solid proof” that Morocco had orchestrated it.

A Spanish police report seen by AFP said the number of Moroccan police officers around the border crossing was “clearly smaller than usual” and that officers “made no serious attempt” to stem the surge.
The report was based on satellite images, open-source videos and testimonies from migrants.

The Spanish government has since had to identify the thousands of migrants who remain in Ceuta to determine whether they are entitled to asylum. Unaccompanied children cannot be summarily deported. — AFP
953f78f2e5abd8de: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here today dismissed environmental watchdog RimbaWatch’s applications for judicial review against two ministries over their alleged failure to investigate complaints concerning the "misleading" marketing of a fossil fuel product.
The applications sought to challenge decisions by the natural resources and environmental sustainability ministry (NRES) and the domestic trade and cost of living ministry (KPDN) last year.
RimbaWatch’s lawyer, Kumaresan Thurairaju, said justice Azizan Md Arshad dismissed the applications in chambers.
The court made no order as to costs.
Kumaresan said RimbaWatch would appeal the ruling and write to the court to request its grounds of judgment.
Senior federal counsel Syahriah Shapiee and Intan Syafinaz Ros’lin appeared for the two ministries, while lawyer Abhilaash Subramaniam appeared as amicus curiae for the Malaysian Bar.

Last year, RimbaWatch lodged complaints with NRES and KPDN over a fossil fuel company regarding the marketing of a product derived from fossil fuels as "carbon neutral", which it claimed was misleading.

RimbaWatch said it filed the complaints with the two ministries because KPDN represented the ministry responsible for consumer protection, while NRES represented the ministry responsible for preventing pollution and protecting the environment.
"We suggest that, if indeed these claims are misleading as we believe, they could harm both consumer protection and climate protection interests," it said.
However, KPDN informed RimbaWatch that the complaint fell outside its jurisdiction and should instead be filed with NRES.
NRES, meanwhile, told RimbaWatch to file the complaint with KPDN.
ee04e2f2dbd5ad63: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 23 — Malaysia and China are strengthening strategic cooperation in the transport sector through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Transport Cooperation, the Ministry of Transport (MOT) said.
In a statement today, MOT said the MoU was signed following a bilateral meeting between Transport Minister Anthony Loke and his Chinese counterpart Liu Wei during Loke’s official visit to Beijing.
“The MoU establishes a formal framework for bilateral strategic cooperation covering land, rail, maritime and air transport, as well as the logistics sector.

“Among the areas of focus are the exchange of technical expertise, capacity building, the use of artificial intelligence technology, green transport and the development of low-carbon infrastructure,” it said.

At the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on efforts to expand strategic cooperation in the transport sector and enhance the connectivity, efficiency and sustainability of the transport systems of both countries.

The statement said the cooperation is expected to enhance Malaysia’s capacity in policymaking, strengthen supply chain efficiency, attract Chinese technology investments and, in turn, strengthen Malaysia’s role as a regional transport hub for Asean.

Loke also witnessed the signing of an MoU on Civil Aviation Safety Cooperation between the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) and the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC), which was signed by CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud and CAAC deputy administrator Hu Zhenjiang.
“The CAAM-CAAC cooperation covers the approval of qualifications, certification and oversight of aviation organisations, licensing and oversight of flight operations.

“The MoU will help strengthen Malaysia’s civil aviation safety standards, reduce duplication in technical processes and facilitate the movement of aeronautical products and services between the two countries,” it said.

According to MOT, Loke also paid a courtesy call on National Railway Administration of China administrator Song Xiude to exchange views on the development and regulation of the rail sector, operational safety, capacity building and the use of technology in rail systems.

“The visit reflects the close and mature relations between Malaysia and China, as well as the commitment of both countries to translate those relations into practical, high-impact and mutually beneficial transport cooperation,” MOT said. — Bernama
a4d55137f333c864: KUALA LUMPUR: Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim menyelesaikan saman fitnah difailkan tiga tahun lalu terhadap Ahli Parlimen Pendang Awang Hashim.

Peguam Anwar, Sankara Nair, memaklumkan Mahkamah Tinggi bahawa kedua pihak bersetuju menyelesaikan pertikaian tersebut secara baik, dengan Anwar menarik balik saman itu tanpa kebebasan memfailkan semula dan tiada perintah mengenai kos.
Susulan peguam Awang, Yusfarizal Yusoff mengesahkan perkara itu, Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman Roslan Mat Nor membatalkan saman berkenaan mengikut syarat dipersetujui.
Hakim turut melapangkan tarikh perbicaraan yang dijadualkan bulan depan.

Dalam kenyataan bersama yang dikemukakan di mahkamah, kedua pihak menyatakan mereka memutuskan untuk menyelesaikan perkara itu selepas bersetuju bahawa terdapat isu lebih penting yang perlu diberi keutamaan demi kepentingan rakyat dan negara.
Kedua pihak berkata, mereka juga telah mempertimbangkan implikasi prosiding fitnah tersebut, termasuk kos litigasi yang perlu ditanggung.

"Awang Hashim dengan penuh rasa rendah diri dan tanpa bersyarat, menarik balik semua kenyataan dibuat olehnya pada atau sekitar 21 Feb 2023, yang menjadi asas kepada tindakan undang-undang ini, dan bersetuju tidak mengulangi atau menerbitkan semula mana-mana kenyataan sedemikian atau kenyataan membawa maksud sama atau secara substansial serupa, pada masa hadapan," menurut kenyataan itu.

Kedua pihak turut menzahirkan harapan agar penyelesaian itu diterima dan dihormati semua pihak, serta perkara berkenaan tidak lagi dipolitikkan atau dijadikan bahan yang boleh menjejaskan keharmonian, perpaduan, dan kestabilan negara.

Anwar memfailkan saman terbabit pada Mac 2023 berhubung kenyataan didakwa dibuat Awang pada sidang media di luar Dewan Rakyat pada 21 Feb tahun itu, mengenai pelantikan Anwar sebagai perdana menteri dan tuduhan pendakwaan terpilih.
07ed5f9073213df9: TOKYO: China's 13-year-old swimmer Yu Zidi went fastest in the heats as she closes in on a hattrick of Asian Games golds on Wednesday - and her teammates say her stunning success is no longer a surprise.
Yu has already won two golds in Tokyo in Games-record times and will go for a third title in the women's 400m individual medley after posting the fastest time in qualifying with 4min 39.43sec.
The schoolgirl has been the talk of swimming since becoming the youngest medallist in world championships history last year with bronze for China's relay team aged just 12.
She is shaping up to be a major medal threat at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.
Teammate Zhang Yufei, a multiple Olympic gold medallist and world champion who was named the women's MVP of the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou, said nothing Yu does is shocking any more.
"Everyone is thinking, 'Wow, what will her next result be? What will she do in her next competition?'," said Zhang, now 28.
"Expectations have become bigger than surprise. I hope she can withstand that pressure."
Yu controlled her 400m IM heat from start to finish and topped qualifying 0.36sec ahead of Japan's Mio Narita.
Yu has already won the 200m butterfly and 200m IM events this week.
Zhang, who won the 10th Asian Games gold of her career this week with China's 4x100m freestyle relay team, said she was "quite shocked" when Yu first burst onto the scene.
"I only see her at the domestic trials and major international competitions each year," said Zhang.
"But every time I see her compete, I can see that she has improved again, and that makes me very happy."
Yu's success at the Asian Games has caused a sensation back home in China.
Her back story, such as being spotted by chance by a swimming coach at a water park, and her struggle with interviews, has gone viral.
Zhang believes Yu has the potential to become the standard-bearer of Chinese swimming.
"I hope this young girl can continue to maintain this momentum and give Chinese swimming hope," she said.
"We also want to see just how far she can go in the future."
ace14a4a3fa11f01: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Police have opened an investigation into Mandiri Development Centre Sdn Bhd over funds suspected to be proceeds from unlawful activities received between 2024 and 2026.

The police said the Anti‑Money Laundering Criminal Investigation Team at Bukit Aman initiated the probe on September 10 following a police report lodged after a review of the company, according to a press statement issued this morning.

“Police will continue to conduct a thorough investigation in accordance with the law against any party suspected of being linked to the case,” Inspector‑General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said.
He said the investigation covers the storage, transfer, use and movement of money suspected to be connected to unlawful activities.
Police said two Mandiri directors were arrested at about 3.53pm on September 22 at the Anti‑Money Laundering Investigation Office in Jalan Tun Razak to assist in the investigation.
The case is being investigated under Section 4(1) of the Anti‑Money Laundering, Anti‑Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001.
Khalid reminded the public not to speculate or spread unverified information about the ongoing investigation.
He said inaccurate statements could mislead the public and disrupt the investigation process.
Khalid said police would ensure the investigation is conducted professionally, transparently and in accordance with the law.
3489ee50ea1e18fe: SINGAPORE, Sept 23 — The upgraded Asean Trade in Goods Agreement (Atiga) is expected to take effect by end-2026, ahead of the original mid-2027, said Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong.

Gan, who is also Trade and Industry Minister, said the decision was made at the 58th Asean Economic Ministers’ (AEM) Meeting and Related Meetings in Manila, the Philippines, where member countries agreed to ratify it earlier.
“We are now planning to bring it forward to this year. We are working hard with our fellow Asean members to race to the end and to cross the line before the end of the year.
“We are optimistic that we will be able to do so,” he told the media in Singapore yesterday.
Gan said the agreement will significantly facilitate intra-Asean trade by simplifying and clarifying rules for businesses to operate within Asean.

“At the same time, it will also make Asean a very important and very attractive destination for investment, because investors know that in Asean they will be able to trade within Asean freely,” he said.

Singapore’s Trade and Industry Ministry said in a statement that the decision demonstrates Asean’s resolve to keep markets open and respond collectively to external shocks and supply chain disruptions.
Early implementation will help businesses reap its benefits sooner through smoother trade flows, improved customs procedures and reduced friction when trading across the region, it said.

The ministry said that, among others, AEM also laid the groundwork to review the Asean Trade in Services Agreement and moved towards implementing the recently concluded Asean Digital Economy Framework Agreement.
“Ministers advanced preparatory work towards a potential Asean Green Economy Framework Agreement to support the development of an interoperable Asean carbon market,” it said. — Bernama
7b5e8bfbb57eda01: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has settled a defamation suit filed three years ago against Pendang MP Awang Hashim.

Anwar’s lawyer, SN Nair, informed the High Court today that the parties had agreed to resolve the dispute amicably, with Anwar withdrawing the suit without liberty to file afresh and no order as to costs.
After confirmation of this by Awang’s lawyer, Yusfarizal Yusoff, judicial commissioner Roslan Mat Nor struck out the suit on the agreed terms.
The judge also vacated the trial dates scheduled for next month.

In a joint statement tendered in court, the parties said they decided to resolve the matter after agreeing that there were more important issues which should be prioritised in the interests of the people and country.
They said they had also considered the implications of the defamation proceedings, including the litigation costs to be borne by both parties.

"Awang Hashim, with humility and without reservation, withdraws all statements made by him on or around Feb 21, 2023, which formed the basis of this legal action, and agrees not to repeat or republish any such statements, or statements carrying the same or substantially similar meaning, in the future," the statement read.

The parties also expressed hope that the settlement would be accepted and respected by all parties, and that the matter would no longer be politicised or used as material that could affect the harmony, unity and stability of the country.

Anwar filed the suit in March 2023 over remarks allegedly made by Awang at a press conference outside the Dewan Rakyat on Feb 21 that year concerning Anwar’s appointment as prime minister and allegations of selective prosecution.
625a35e540bd3a24: MANILA: Wars in Europe and the Middle East and a severe El Nino are amplifying price pressures across Asia, likely fanning inflation through next year and keeping central banks on guard, according to the Asian Development Bank.

The re-escalation of fighting in Iran and the spread of conflict to Yemen have choked supplies of crude and refined products, while Russia’s war on Ukraine has disrupted grain shipments, the ADB said in its latest outlook released on Wednesday. Abnormal weather patterns due to El Nino are already threatening harvests from India to Thailand, as well as reducing hydropower generation and even restricting traffic in waterways like the Panama Canal.

“Risks remain tilted to the downside,” ADB chief economist Albert Park said in the report. “Further escalation of conflicts or worse than expected El Nino impacts could dent growth and push inflation higher.”

The ADB forecasts inflation for the developing Asia-Pacific region at 4.2% this year and 3.5% next year, both well above the 3% recorded in 2025. It expects economic growth to slow to 5% in 2026, from 5.5%, and raised its oil-price forecasts to US$90 and US$78 a barrel for this year and next.

While broad subsidies have helped cushion the blow for consumers this year, persistently high energy prices have started working their way through economies. That pass-through is likely to be strongest in countries where food weighs heavily in the consumption basket, such as in South Asia, the ADB said.

Several economies have scope for further monetary tightening this year if inflation persists, including Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Vietnam, the bank said. Once inflation recedes, policymakers may start weighing rate cuts in 2027, it said.

“Overall, policy rates are expected to move gradually toward levels observed before the escalation of the Middle East conflict, though the pace and extent of easing will depend on the evolution of inflation, growth, and external risks,” the ADB said.
1cfa6b5ad0f5a065: PETALING JAYA: Ketua Polis Negara Khalid Ismail berkata Mandiri sedang disiasat susulan laporan polis yang mendakwa kumpulan belia itu menerima dana dipercayai hasil aktiviti menyalahi undang-undang sejak 2024 hingga tahun ini.

Khalid berkata, polis membuka siasatan pengubahan wang haram pada 10 Sept di bawah Seksyen 4(1) Akta Pencegahan Pengubahan Wang Haram, Pencegahan Pembiayaan Keganasan dan Hasil Daripada Aktiviti Haram 2001 terhadap Mandiri Development Centre Sdn Bhd.
Seksyen berkenaan memperuntukkan hukuman penjara sehingga 15 tahun serta denda tidak kurang daripada lima kali ganda nilai hasil aktiviti haram atau RM5 juta, mengikut mana-mana yang lebih tinggi.
Pengarah Eksekutif Mandiri Amir Hadi dan Pengarah Kewangannya Dobby Chew ditahan Jabatan Siasatan Jenayah Komersial (JSJK) Bukit Aman semalam bagi membantu siasatan.
Penahanan itu mendapat kritikan daripada kumpulan masyarakat sivil dan beberapa ahli politik DAP yang menggesa Amir dan Chew dibebaskan serta-merta.

“Kami akan terus menjalankan siasatan menyeluruh terhadap mana-mana pihak yang disyaki mempunyai kaitan dengan kes ini, termasuk perkara berkaitan penyimpanan, pemindahan dan penggunaan dana, selain kemasukan atau pengeluaran wang yang disyaki hasil daripada aktiviti menyalahi undang-undang.
“Polis juga memberi jaminan kepada orang ramai bahawa siasatan akan dijalankan secara profesional, telus dan mengikut undang-undang sedia ada,” katanya dalam kenyataan.

Pada 18 Sept, lebih 20 pegawai polis menyerbu sebuah pejabat di Petaling Jaya yang dikongsi Mandiri dan Hayat, sebuah NGO yang diuruskan Chew. Kumpulan berkenaan menyerahkan rekod kewangan, laporan audit, dokumen cukai, rekod gaji kakitangan, sebuah komputer dan pemacu USB yang mengandungi maklumat kewangan.

Siasatan itu menyusuli tindakan penguatkuasaan baru-baru ini terhadap kedua-duanya, termasuk pembekuan akaun bank peribadi dan organisasi di bawah undang-undang pengubahan wang haram serta larangan perjalanan yang menghalang Amir dan Chew daripada ke luar negara.
f5dfd991b521f60b: LONDON, Sept 23 — Four British novels will compete against a Jamaican epic and an American domestic drama for the prestigious Booker Prize, as the judges yesterday unveiled a shortlist of “idiosyncratic” stories.
As artists, politicians and tech leaders around the world sound the alarm about the rapid rise of artificial intelligence, judges of the annual award said they had selected a “very human” shortlist.
“These books, we truly believe, cannot be replicated by artificial intelligence. These are very human books,” said judge and poet Raymond Antrobus.
The six-strong shortlist includes two heavyweight entries by past Booker winners: John of John by Douglas Stuart and Marlon James’s The Disappearers.
Lauded by critics, the over 600-page epic by Caribbean author James follows the survivor of a brutal homophobic attack against a troupe of gay actors in 1980s Kingston.

Scottish-American writer Stuart—who won the Booker in 2020 for Shuggie Bain—returns to the shortlist with his poignant exploration of a father-son bond strained by shame and secrets, set on the far-flung Outer Hebrides in Scotland.

The other shortlisted books include American novelist Elizabeth Strout’s The Things We Never Say, and Brits Luke Kennard Black Bag, M. John Harrison The End of Everything and Rebecca Perry May We Feed the King.
“These novels range from the hilarious to the discomfiting, from the frighteningly strange to the alarmingly domestic,” chair of the judges, classicist Mary Beard said.
The prize was scooped last year by British-Hungarian writer David Szalay for Flesh, which explores themes of male alienation.
This year’s male-heavy shortlist also probes questions of gender roles and sexuality.

“Men are having to rethink their role, I suppose. And that’s reflected in the books that they’re writing,” judge Jarvis Cocker, frontman of the Britpop band Pulp, told reporters ahead of the shortlist announcement.

“When we first started reading, I think it’s fair to say that most of the books we were putting through were by women,” adding Cocker, only half-joking. “It took a while actually to get a book written by a man that seemed good.”

The finalists were selected from a longlist of 13 books, whittled down from 163 submissions for the prize, which celebrates the best long-form fiction by writers of any nationality, written in English and published in the last year.
The winner will be announced on November 9 in a London ceremony.

“We really wanted to build a list that was full of variety, that had lots of things that were idiosyncratic, that might not be universally loved, that might draw a strong opinion,” added Rebecca Liu, a writer and critic.

The End of Everything is an enigmatic, apocalyptic novel set on England’s windswept eastern coast and Strout’s tender Massachusetts-based novel offers a “calm antidote to contemporary events”, according to the Booker judges.
Kennard’s satire follows a struggling actor who gets paid to wear a black leather bag on his head by a psychology professor, while Perry turns to a reluctant medieval king in her debut novel. — AFP
7d3c21bc95c5bf0c: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 11 — Pandan, lemongrass and Bentong ginger are staples of the Malaysian kitchen — not usually the gin glass.
That changed for one evening at 443 Bar Lounge in The Westin Kuala Lumpur, where an intimate masterclass traced how these familiar home flavours ended up in a bottle of craft gin.

Hosted by Gin Malaya co-founder Eu Jin Foong and brand ambassador Callan Green, the session walked guests through the spirit’s origins in 2022, when a shared love of food led its founders to ask what a gin inspired by Malaysia might actually taste like.
Two years of experimentation followed, translating ingredients deeply embedded in local cooking into a spirit that remains recognisably gin, yet distinctly its own.
“When we first started developing Gin Malaya, we kept coming back to flavours we knew — pandan, lemongrass, ginger — and asking how they can translate into a gin,” said Eu Jin in a statement.
The gin itself brings together hand-foraged Highland juniper with lemongrass, pandan and Bentong ginger — a pairing of Scottish distilling tradition with a Malaysian botanical profile.
“There is something quite special about watching someone recognise those flavours in the glass. They are familiar, but presented in a way they may never have experienced before.”
The gin itself brings together hand-foraged Highland juniper with lemongrass, pandan and Bentong ginger — a pairing of Scottish distilling tradition with a Malaysian botanical profile.

Guests at the masterclass also worked through a line-up of signature cocktails built around those flavours: the Malaya Rock, a light, refreshing mix of pandan and coconut water served over ice; The Torch, combining muddled bunga kantan with Campari and lemon for a bittersweet sour; the Pandan Malaya, shaken with pandan and smoked ginger and tinted violet with butterfly pea; and the Kantan Fizz, a straightforward build of gin, lemon and soda.
The cocktail collection is now available at The Westin Kuala Lumpur, with drinks priced at RM45 nett.

Founded in 2022 and launched in Malaysia in 2024, Gin Malaya has since picked up international recognition, including a one-star Great Taste Award in 2025 — judged through blind tasting — and a Bronze Medal at the London Spirits Competition.
The brand is now sold in both Malaysia and the United Kingdom.
a4e43b66ce891204: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Malaysia has proposed a science‑driven framework and long‑term funding mechanism to strengthen Asean’s efforts in addressing transboundary haze under the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP).

The science‑driven framework refers to Science Diplomacy, which would allow Asean countries to jointly use scientific data, research and expertise, while the long‑term funding mechanism involves a Sustainable Haze Fund to support monitoring, fire prevention, research and haze‑control activities.

The proposals were raised by Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup at the 27th Sub‑Regional Ministerial Steering Committee on Transboundary Haze Pollution meeting in Bali recently, according to the New Straits Times.
“The approach is expected to strengthen regional cooperation and support science‑ and evidence‑based policy and decision‑making,” Arthur said.

He said Science Diplomacy would help translate shared scientific findings into coordinated regional policies and operational decisions, while the Sustainable Haze Fund would provide continuous financing for long‑term haze‑mitigation efforts.
He said the meeting agreed that the Asean Secretariat should study the feasibility of Science Diplomacy and explore ways to increase contributions to and use of the Asean Haze Fund under the AATHP.
Arthur said long‑term solutions required sustained cooperation and commitment from all member states under the agreement, which was signed 24 years ago.
He said the AATHP emphasised cooperation, mutual respect, national sovereignty and consensus‑based decision‑making rather than punitive measures.
Arthur said each member state must fulfil its responsibilities, particularly in preventing and controlling fires within its borders to avoid affecting neighbouring countries.

He said Malaysia would present a stronger position on haze management at the Committee Meeting and Conference of the Parties to the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution in Vietnam this November.
Arthur said environment ministers and senior officials from all Asean member states attended the annual meeting to review the haze situation and preventive measures.

556a3f7ce7c4e744: The day I landed in New Delhi for the BRICS summit, there was already chatter on Indian television about how much the whole thing cost.

On one channel, presenter Arnab Goswami wondered whether critics expected Vladimir Putin to be put up in Paharganj, Delhi’s famously chaotic budget-hotel quarter -- imagine the old Pudu area of Kuala Lumpur crossed with Penang’s backpacker-quarter Chulia Street, then add several thousand people, several thousand horns and the distinct possibility that your taxi driver knows a shortcut which somehow takes longer.

The debate also introduced me to the useful Hindi expression “naraz fufa”, for the perpetually offended uncle at a family gathering who can always find something wrong. The BJP, India's ruling party, had used it while responding to opposition leader P Chidambaram, who had questioned what India was actually getting out of BRICS.

Malaysia has no shortage of the same uncle. We just never bothered giving him such an efficient name. Ours generally lives in the family WhatsApp group, where he specialises in multiple question marks and information forwarded by somebody’s cousin in Johor.

Still, the grumpy uncle has a point. Malaysians have also asked what we get from hosting large international gatherings, with their convoys, security cordons, hotel bills and dinners involving more cutlery than most of us own at home. The Asean summit in Kuala Lumpur last year prompted the same questions, and they are perfectly fair ones.
After following Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim around India for several days, I found myself asking pretty much the same thing.

There was no shortage of official business. Anwar and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed trade, investment, semiconductors, tourism, education and various other matters that normally arrive in press statements wearing their best bureaucratic attire.
Malaysia's singing PM
Yet the thing many ordinary Indians seemed to notice was Anwar singing Kishore Kumar.

His rendition travelled across Indian television and social media, reaching people who would probably never willingly read a BRICS declaration. Malaysians had seen something similar when Donald Trump arrived for the Asean summit in Kuala Lumpur last year and briefly danced along with traditional performers at KLIA, with Anwar joining him for a few seconds.
It is a reminder that governments can spend weeks drafting language about “people-to-people ties”, only for an old Hindi song or a slightly awkward dance to do considerably more work.

But summit diplomacy eventually has to produce something more durable than a viral clip, and one of the conversations that interested me most in Delhi was with Arun Rajendran of Segula Technologies, a French engineering company with a large operation in India.

His explanation was refreshingly free of ceremony. Experienced engineers in India were becoming more expensive, while Malaysia already had much of the manufacturing base needed to take on more specialised engineering work. If we trained enough people properly, some of that work could eventually move here.
That caught my attention far more than another discussion about the world order. In other words, a company was saying that there could be better engineering jobs here if we got the skills right.
That is something a parent with a child studying engineering can understand without first having to Google “multipolarity”.

Other Indian businesses were looking at Malaysia too, including companies already buying large amounts of our palm oil and others interested in using Malaysia as a base for Southeast Asia. Of course, meetings are not investments, announcements are not jobs, and handshakes - however firm - remain surprisingly difficult to deposit at a bank.
That is why the real test comes later.
Malayalee connection

Then we flew south to Kerala (now known as Keralam), where the mood changed completely. After several days of giant conference halls, security checks and enough accreditation tags to start a small stationery business, Anwar was talking about old friends, Malayalee lawyers and the centuries-old links between the Malabar coast and the Malay world.

At Markaz in Kozhikode, he slipped two Malayalam words into his speech: “Entha varthanam?” (roughly, “What’s up?”) The crowd responded immediately. At another gathering, he noticed that what had been advertised as a high-tea appeared, at that moment, to consist mainly of water, briefly raising the prospect of a diplomatic incident over missing beverages.

Then came the Malayalee jokes. Anwar recalled the lawyers who had stood by him during the difficult years of his political career, before suggesting that one Malayalee weakness was not knowing when to stop talking. This was a bold complaint from a politician who happened to be holding a microphone.
After the crowds that greeted him, he even joked about contesting an election in Kerala. Tambun, as far as we know, remains safe.

I also discovered a Malabar porotta with a faint coconut-oil finish that was so good it made a more persuasive argument for closer Malaysia-India relations than several official speeches I had heard that week.

Behind the jokes and the food, however, was something more substantial. Anwar spoke about the movement of people, religion, culture and trade between the Malabar coast and the Malay world over centuries. Those connections existed long before BRICS, Asean or anyone decided that every relationship between two countries required the word “strategic” somewhere in the description.
What really matters

Perhaps that is the better way to look at these summits. They provide the room, get leaders and businesses in front of one another and give officials a chance to push things along. Cultural familiarity helps too. A Kishore Kumar song may open a door which another 12-page joint statement merely leans against.
But eventually, the naraz fufa is entitled to come back and ask what happened next.

Six months or a year from now, did Segula create those engineering jobs? Did more Indian companies invest here? Did Malaysian businesses find new customers in India? Did talks about tourism lead to more flights and visitors?
Those are better measures of success than the length of a motorcade or the grandeur of a summit venue.
Putin might not be checking into Paharganj any time soon. The rest of us are still entitled to ask what was left behind after he checked out.
Predeep Nambiar is FMT’s northern region bureau chief.

3045dc127697ef6f: From Saida Abu Bakar
Reform should move a health system from where it is now to somewhere better for the people who depend on it.
It is not simply about changing structures, introducing new programmes or asking institutions to work differently.

That is why health reform needs patient partnership. Within one healthcare ecosystem, two realities operate at the same time: the institutional system, which is how healthcare is organised and delivered, and the patient system, which is how healthcare is experienced and navigated.

A pathway can look complete institutionally and still feel fragmented to the person moving through it. Institutions understand policy, professional practice and how services are organised; patients and carers understand what happens when all of that meets real life — where care connects, where it breaks and where responsibility becomes unclear.

Both perspectives are needed if reform is supposed to work outside the meeting room. We often hear that major healthcare reforms take years, sometimes even a generation, before their full impact can be seen.

That may be true, but time should not become the explanation in itself. If change takes that long, the system should understand why — where progress is being held back, where responsibility changes hands and what could have been identified earlier.
The mechanism matters. We would not redesign clinical care without clinical expertise or change healthcare financing without financial and policy expertise.

The same principle should apply to the patient journey. Implementation may take years, but patient partnership should begin on day one. If patients only appear at the end, when the system finally asks whether they benefited, we risk discovering too late what could have been understood much earlier.

Opening reform to patients does not take authority away from institutions. It gives decision-makers a fuller view of the system they are trying to change. You cannot fairly redesign a journey while leaving out the people who actually have to travel through it.

But bringing a patient into the room is not, by itself, patient partnership. Participation, representation and partnership are different things. A person can speak from personal experience without claiming to represent anyone else.

An organisation may nominate someone to carry its position. Representing a wider community is different; there must be clarity about who that community is, what mandate is being carried and how information goes back.

A seat at the table creates participation. A mandate is what creates representation. The same standard should apply across healthcare. A clinician brings clinical expertise but does not automatically represent an entire profession.
A researcher may contribute knowledge without speaking for every researcher. An organisation may have years of experience without representing every group affected by an issue.
There is also no single patient voice. The people needed for healthcare financing may not be the same people needed for digital health, workforce reform, patient safety or access to care.

The stronger approach is to bring the relevant people into the relevant decision while there is still room for their experience to shape how the problem is understood and what success should look like.
Their knowledge should sit alongside professional judgement, research, operational realities and practical constraints.

Partnership does not mean everyone agrees, and it does not mean every recommendation must be accepted. What matters is that the route is visible: input is considered, decisions are made by those with the proper authority, responsibility for implementation is clear, and the people who contributed eventually hear what happened.
Measure. Learn. Respond. Improve. Then report back.

Without that return journey, engagement remains one-way. People share their experience, the meeting ends and the system moves on. A meaningful partnership mechanism should connect lived experience to deliberation, decisions, implementation, outcomes and feedback.
This is also where resilience and leadership come together.

A resilient health system is not only one that keeps operating through workforce shortages, funding pressures, supply disruptions or emergencies; it is one that can adapt without losing the patient journey between institutions.

That requires workforce, financing, infrastructure and technology, but the way reform is led has to evolve too. Leadership needs to look beyond individual organisational boundaries, understand where responsibilities connect and keep accountability visible across the whole journey.

Patients and families should not have to become the coordinators of the health system simply because their care crosses several services. Nor should “people-centred” mean inviting people to comment after the important decisions have already been made.

Patient partnership is not asking patients to take over the roles of policymakers, clinicians or institutions. It is about strengthening reform with something institutions cannot generate on their own: the experience of actually living through the system.

If Malaysia wants reform that is genuinely resilient, patient representation cannot remain an engagement activity sitting at the side. It needs a credible place from the beginning — in understanding what is not working, shaping what “better” should look like, testing whether change works in real life and learning from what happens afterwards.

Reform may take years, even generations, but that makes the mechanism more important, not less. The longer the journey, the more important it is to know that we are solving the right problems with the right people and learning as we go.

We can redesign the aircraft, change the route, strengthen the workforce and improve the technology. But before asking people to board another reform, there is one final test: the passengers are ready — is the system ready for the journey?
Saida Abu Bakar is an independent patient advocate working on patient partnership and health systems.

29ee8acaf2f6d9dc: Ia berlaku di Johor, berlaku juga di Negeri Sembilan. Adakah ia akan berlaku di Melaka? Saya bercakap mengenai apa yang saya anggap 'politik identiti' dalam pilihan raya sebelum ini.

"Apa yang berlaku di PRN Johor dan Negeri Sembilan menjelaskan satu dapatan yang begitu menarik tapi hakikatnya menggusarkan," kata seorang kawan yang membuat tinjauan di dua PRN berkenaan. Kata kuncinya ialah 'menggusarkan'.

Seterusnya, kata kawan saya, "politik asalnya bergerak dari idea reformasi atau perubahan kembali ke pangkuan identiti". Semasa artikel ini ditulis, pengumuman mengenai pembubaran DUN Melaka baru saja dibuat maka tentulah persoalan di minda saya ialah adakah yang 'menggusarkan' akan berlaku di Melaka.

Terus terang saya tidak suka politik identiti. Tetapi menurut profesor di Jabatan Sains Politik dan Pengajian Madani Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia, Zainal Abidin Sanusi, ada beberapa aspek serta interpretasi mengenai 'politik identiti'.

Siapalah saya untuk mempertikai seorang ahli akademik maka ada eloknya saya tidak menggunakan istilah 'politik identiti' untuk penulisan ini. Namun menegaskan apa yang saya kata tadi ialah saya tidak suka taktik politikus mengambil sesuatu perkara untuk dijadikan isu perkauman, di samping meniup atau membakar sentimen ras untuk mendapat sokongan di peti undi.
Mungkin istilah tepat untuk saya gunakan ialah 'politik perkauman'. Istilah ini dulu sering digunakan.
Berbalik kepada kawan saya tadi yang meninjau PRN Johor dan Negeri Sembilan pada Julai dan Ogos lalu. Kata beliau:
"Tanah ini milik Melayu, kami orang asal, yang lain adalah pendatang, jangan besar kepala, sedarlah hidup menumpang. Semua konotasi ini jelas kedengaran dalam siri kempen, penerangan dan serangan."

Menurut pemerhati politik ada juga terjadi semasa kempen di Negeri Sembilan, apabila pemimpin DAP iaitu Loke Siew Fook dituduh mahu jadi menteri besar meskipun tidak benar. Tetapi ada pengundi termakan kata-kata bohong itu.
Bak kata kawan saya, frasa berbaur provokatif bergulir lalu berkembang menjadi sentimen yang dipegang dan naratif yang dipercayai sehingga berjaya mencipta gelombang yang membadai dua negeri itu.
Hampir pasti politikus yang main game itu akan main game serupa di Melaka.

Seorang kawan menarik perhatian saya kepada buku 'Identity: The Demand for Dignity and the Politics of Resentment' oleh penulis Amerika Syarikat, Francis Fukuyama. Buku itu menurut kawan saya berhujah bahawa politik hari ini bukan lagi sekadar perebutan kekayaan tetapi perebutan untuk diiktiraf sebagai tuan.
Namun, di negara yang ada konsep 'Ketuanan Melayu' bukankah orang Melayu sememangnya 'tuan'? Jadi apa yang nak dibimbangkan?
Bagi saya, yang mahu menjadi tuan ialah politikus dan mereka bergerak atas nama Melayu untuk menghalalkan taktik mereka.

Di Israel ada konsep 'Ketuanan Yahudi'. Carian Google memberitahu bahawa politik identiti di Israel berpusat pada usaha menentukan sifat negara itu sebagai sebuah entiti bangsa dan agama Yahudi, di samping berdepan perpecahan kaum, aliran, agama, dan status minoriti Arab.

Politik Israel didominasi parti-parti Zionis yang mendaulatkan identiti Yahudi dari segi bangsa dan agama, manakala parti-parti agama bukan Zionis memainkan peranan penting dalam gabungan kerajaan serta menuntut keistimewaan dan pelaksanaan nilai-nilai agama dalam undang-undang sivil.

Bekas diplomat Israel, Shlomo Ben-Ami, menulis untuk The Strategist pada Sept 2018: "Israel chooses identity over democracy". Penganalisis politik Palestin, Ehab Jabareen, menerusi kolum di Al Jazeera berkata, "Israel's religious right is changing the state from within".

Pada 16 Ogos lalu, Al Jazeera melaporkan Itamar Ben-Gvir si pemimpin berhaluan paling kanan yang memegang jawatan menteri keselamatan dalam pentadbiran Benjamin Netanyahu berkata tentera Israel perlu bunuh 30 atau 40 rakyat Palestin di Gaza setiap malam.
Semua itu untuk menunjukkan kehebatan ketuanan Israel. Netanyahu juga menggunakan serangan harian ke atas Gaza dan Tebing Barat dan perang Iran sebagai lambang kekuatan Israel menjaga rakyatnya.

Yang sering dilaungkan ialah hanya pemimpin yang kuat boleh mengangkat bangsa Yahudi dan menangkis ancaman terhadap rakyatnya. Bolehlah dijangka cakap-cakap besar dan tindakan kejam akan dipertingkatkan menjelang pilihan raya Israel pada 27 Oktober ini.
Keadaan di Malaysia tidak seburuk itu meskipun ada politikus kita yang main taktik ketuanan, kehebatan bangsa dan mempertahankan agama untuk menang pilihan raya.
Lantas, eloklah kita elokkan keadaan untuk memastikan keburukan di Israel tidak akan terjadi di negara ini sampai bila-bila pun.
